1	---
2	title: "Tools: multicam"
3	description: The agent tools that copy pieces of a clip to another track, re-pick a shot from another camera and cut a Program track by who is talking, with every argument, answer and refusal.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These three tools cut between synced cameras: `copy_pieces` copies stretches of a clip onto another track at the same times, `switch_angle` re-picks one shot from another camera, and `switch_by_speaker` cuts a whole Program track from who is talking.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸', 'Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…']}
12	  tools={['copy_pieces', 'switch_angle', 'switch_by_speaker']}
13	  needs="Nothing to set up. When there's only one microphone, faces are read on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
14	/>
15	
16	Times are in ticks, 600,000 a second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). [Set up several cameras](/multicam/set-up/) says how the tracks should be laid out first.
17	
18	## `copy_pieces`
19	
20	Copies pieces of a clip onto another track at the same project times. It has no menu item of its own: it's what [**Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**](/multicam/switch-angle/) writes with. An agent can cut a whole program with one `copy_pieces` per camera clip. See [Copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/).
21	
22	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
23	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
24	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to copy pieces of. |
25	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track the pieces land on. It must be free over every range. |
26	| `ranges` | array of `[from, to]` pairs | Yes | The stretches to copy, in project times, inside the clip and not overlapping. At least one pair. |
27	| `video` | boolean | No | Sets each piece's picture on or off. Default: the clip's own setting. |
28	| `audio` | boolean | No | Sets each piece's sound on or off. Default: the clip's own setting. |
29	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside that nest, where the times and tracks are the nest's. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
30	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
31	
32	Each piece is exactly what two splits at its range's ends would leave in the middle: the same source frames at the same times, with speed, a ramp, reversal, a graphic's own timeline, timed words and actions cut as a split cuts them. So a piece of a synced camera shows that camera's own frame at every time. Pieces get new ids, no transition and no link.
33	
34	This call copies the stretches from 0 to 2 s and from 5 to 7 s of clip 5 onto track 3:
35	
36	```json
37	{ "clip": 5, "track": 3, "ranges": [[0, 1200000], [3000000, 4200000]] }
38	```
39	
40	Each range's ends snap to the frame grid, a pair written backwards is the same range, and a range that's empty on the grid is skipped. Ranges may touch. If every range is empty, nothing changes.
41	
42	It answers `ok: true`, `new_clips` (the pieces) and the `project` summary. It's one undo step, **Copy Pieces**.
43	
44	An unknown clip or track stops the call, and so does an empty `ranges`. Then it's refused, with nothing changed, in this order:
45	
46	1. The clip is a nest clip, because a piece of it would replay the nest from its first frame.
47	2. A range is outside the clip.
48	3. Two ranges overlap.
49	4. The destination track is locked.
50	5. The destination track holds a clip over a range. The sentence names that clip and its ends.
51	
52	## `switch_angle`
53	
54	Re-picks one shot from another camera, as [**Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**](/multicam/switch-angle/) does.
55	
56	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
57	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
58	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The shot to re-pick: a clip on the program track. |
59	| `angle` | integer | Yes | The id of the track to re-pick it from. |
60	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
61	
62	An angle is a track whose video clips cover the shot's whole span. A clip with its picture off, or on a hidden track, still counts. The menu lists at most nine angles, and the tool can name any track.
63	
64	The shot is deleted and the angle copied over the same span, one piece per angle clip the span crosses, each with the shot's picture and sound settings. Where two angle clips overlap, the later one takes over at its own start. The clips either side are trimmed back to their old edges, so a dissolve on either edge is formed again with its kind, curve and sound shape.
65	
66	The shot's grade, punch-in, actions and other settings don't carry over.
67	
68	It takes no `scope`. It works in the nest `set_scope` has open.
69	
70	| Key | What it holds |
71	| --- | --- |
72	| `ok` | `true`. |
73	| `step` | **Switch Angle**, or **Switch Angle (transition removed)** when a dissolve couldn't be formed again against a short piece and was dropped. |
74	| `pieces` | The new clip ids, in time order. |
75	| `transitions_removed` | How many dissolves were dropped, from 0 to 2. |
76	| `project` | The summary. |
77	
78	It's one undo step, named as `step` says. An unknown clip or track stops the call. It's refused, with nothing changed, when:
79	
80	- the angle is the shot's own track
81	- the shot's track is locked
82	- the shot is linked to its detached sound
83	- the angle doesn't cover the shot. The sentence names the first tick with nothing to show.
84	- an edge is held short of where it needs to go, for example by a speed ramp. The sentence names the clip and the tick it reached.
85	- one of the edits that make up the re-pick can't be made. The sentence is that edit's own.
86	
87	## `switch_by_speaker`
88	
89	Cuts a Program track from synced cameras, showing whoever talks on each microphone, as [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) does. Run [`sync_audio`](/mcp/tools-audio/#sync_audio) first, because it trusts where the clips sit. Then select the clips with [`set_selection`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_selection), because it reads the selected clips.
90	
91	It takes no `scope`. It works in the nest `set_scope` has open.
92	
93	### Switch by Speaker options
94	
95	Every argument is optional. [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/) explains the ones the sheet shows.
96	
97	| Argument | Type | What it does |
98	| --- | --- | --- |
99	| `speakers` | array of `{mic, angle}` | Who is who: one object per person, both track ids. A camera's detached sound may be a `mic`. One `mic` named for two or more cameras is [faces mode](#faces-mode). Default: the pairing the selection implies. |
100	| `wide` | integer or null | The camera shown when nobody or everybody talks, or null for none. It must be one of the cameras. Default: the one camera no speaker uses, when exactly one is left. With one microphone and no `speakers`, every camera is a speaker, so there's none. |
101	| `from` | integer | The range's start, in ticks. Give it with `to`. |
102	| `to` | integer | The range's end, after `from`. Give it with `from`. |
103	| `min_shot` | number | Seconds. A shorter shot merges into a neighbour. 0.5 to 30. Default 2, or 3 in faces mode. |
104	| `min_turn` | number | Seconds. A shorter turn, such as a reply, starts no shot. 0.2 to 10. Default 1. The sheet doesn't show it. |
105	| `lead` | number | Seconds a cut comes before the new speaker's first word. 0 to 1. Default 0.2. |
106	| `crosstalk` | string | What a second or more of crosstalk shows: `wide`, or `hold` to stay on the current speaker. Default `wide`. |
107	| `bleed_db` | number | How many dB below a speaker's own level counts as the other person's voice bleeding in, never a turn. 3 to 40. Default 15. |
108	| `dominance_db` | number | How many dB one active microphone must lead every other to count alone. 0 to 30. Default 8. The sheet doesn't show it. |
109	| `wide_after` | number or null | Seconds. Once one person has held the screen this long, cut to the wide for `min_shot`. 2 to 600. Default null, which is off. |
110	| `mute_cameras` | boolean | Turns the cameras' own sound off inside the range. Default: on when no microphone is a camera. |
111	| `track` | integer | Replaces the shots on this track, an earlier Program track, instead of adding one. It must be unlocked, in front of the cameras, hold no selected clip, and hold only pieces of the cameras over the range. |
112	| `apply` | boolean | `false` answers without editing. See [Preview with `apply: false`](#preview-with-apply-false). Default `true`. |
113	| `project` | string | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
114	
115	A number outside its range stops the call and says the range, where the sheet would pull it back in.
116	
117	This call plans a cut with longer shots that stays on the current speaker during crosstalk, without editing anything:
118	
119	```json
120	{ "min_shot": 3, "crosstalk": "hold", "apply": false }
121	```
122	
123	### What it reads
124	
125	- **The cameras:** a camera is a track holding a selected clip with a picture.
126	- **The microphones:** by default these are the tracks holding a selected sound-only clip. With none, each camera with sound is its own microphone. Microphones are paired with cameras front to back, and a track you name in `speakers` still needs a selected clip with its sound on.
127	- **The range:** `from` and `to`, else the In–Out range, else the extent of the selected camera clips.
128	
129	It reads each microphone's loudness and speech, which Frame Job measures when a file is added. Then it cuts a shot `lead` before each new speaker's turn, holds through short replies and silence, shows the wide during crosstalk, and merges shots under `min_shot`.
130	
131	### What it writes
132	
133	It's one undo step, **Switch by Speaker**:
134	
135	- a new track named **Program** directly in front of the front-most camera, or with `track`, that track cleared over the range
136	- one [`copy_pieces`](#copy_pieces) for each camera clip a shot crosses, picture on and sound off
137	- the camera tracks hidden, or, when a camera track holds clips outside the range, its clips split at the range's ends with their pictures off inside
138	- with `mute_cameras`, the cameras' own sound off inside the range, never on a microphone's track
139	
140	Nothing outside the range changes, and the microphones are never edited. A selected clip that gets split keeps both halves selected.
141	
142	### What it answers
143	
144	| Key | What it holds |
145	| --- | --- |
146	| `ok` | `true`. |
147	| `applied` | Whether the project was edited. |
148	| `step` | **Switch by Speaker**. Only when applied. |
149	| `track` | The Program track's id. Null when not applied and no `track` was named. |
150	| `shots` | Each shot's `angle`, `start` and `end`. |
151	| `ops` | How many edits it makes. |
152	| `added` | How many clips it adds. |
153	| `speakers` | The pairing used, each `mic` and `angle`. |
154	| `wide` | The wide camera, or null. |
155	| `mute_cameras` | The value used. |
156	| `mode` | `microphones` or `faces`. |
157	| `note` | Faces mode only: "Faces guess who is talking; check the cuts." |
158	| `project` | The summary. |
159	
160	### Preview with `apply: false`
161	
162	Pass `apply: false` to see the planned shots without editing the project. The answer has the same keys, with `applied` false and no `step`. It's the same work as a real run, so it stops for the same reasons.
163	
164	### Faces mode
165	
166	When one microphone is shared by two or more cameras, their faces decide who talks. This is the default when the selection holds exactly one microphone, and you also get it by naming one `mic` for two or more cameras. See [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/).
167	
168	While the microphone hears speech, each camera's on-device face analysis says whose mouth moves most, going by the largest face in the picture. A camera wins with 1.5 times the next camera's movement, and otherwise it counts as crosstalk.
169	
170	- A named `wide` takes no part in deciding who talks. If you name it without `speakers`, that camera stops being a speaker when it shares a microphone.
171	- `min_shot` defaults to 3.
172	- `mode` says `faces`, and `note` says the cuts are a guess, so check them.
173	
174	Where **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** would show its **Analyzing** sheet, the tool finds the faces it still needs and waits up to 60 s. Past that it's refused, and what it covered is kept. Call it again to continue.
175	
176	### Switch by Speaker refusals
177	
178	Nothing changes when a call is refused. It stops first on a value it can't read, such as an unknown track, a `wide` that isn't a camera, only one of `from` and `to`, or a `to` not after `from`.
179	
180	These are checked together, and the sentence names every one that applies:
181	
182	- fewer than two cameras, or more than nine
183	- a speaker without a microphone or without a camera
184	- one microphone for two speakers, outside faces mode
185	- a microphone still being analysed, or with no speech in the range
186	- speech detection isn't available on this Mac
187	- a camera whose faces are still being found, or that shows no face whose mouth can be read
188	- a stretch no camera covers
189	
190	These each stop the call on their own:
191	
192	- a faces analysis that failed, was stopped, or didn't finish within the wait
193	- the project or the open nest changed during the wait
194	- more clips than the project may hold. Raise `min_shot` to make fewer shots.
195	- a `track` that can't take the shots: it's locked, it holds a selected clip, it isn't in front of the cameras, it has nothing in the range, or it holds a clip that isn't a piece of a camera
196	- a camera clip linked by **Detach Audio**. Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first.

2	title: Camera layouts
3	description: Switch a screen recording and the camera in front of it between corner, side-by-side, stacked and full-frame layouts as it plays.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A camera layout decides how a camera clip and the screen recording behind it share the frame. Choose one at any moment and the picture eases into it there, so a tutorial can go from a small corner camera to a full-frame talking head and back as it plays.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸"
13	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Layout"
14	  tools="switch_layout"
15	/>
16	
17	## Switch the layout
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Move the playhead to where the switch should start.
22	
23	2. Tell Frame Job which clips to use. With nothing selected it looks for the track named "Camera", which is where a recording's camera lands, so usually there's nothing to do. Otherwise select the camera, or the camera and the screen. See [Which clips](#which-clips).
24	
25	3. Choose a layout from **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**.
26	
27	</Steps>
28	
29	To change layout again later, move the playhead on and choose another. To undo a switch, press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd>: one undo step, **Camera Layout**, takes the whole switch back. These items have no keyboard shortcut.
30	
31	The [Layout section](/framing/layout-section/) in the inspector does the same thing for one selected clip, with a switch length you choose. To start a recording in a layout, [choose it in the recorder panel](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/#choose-a-layout) before you record.
32	
33	## The layouts
34	
35	The submenu holds **Corner ▸**, **Rounded Corner ▸** and **Circle ▸**, each with **Bottom Right**, **Bottom Left**, **Top Right** and **Top Left**, then **Side by Side**, **Stacked**, **Camera Full** and **Screen Only**.
36	
37	In the three corner layouts, Camera Full and Screen Only, the screen goes to its full placement. That's where **Add Clip** puts a new clip: centred, and scaled down to fit when it's bigger than the canvas and **Fit new clips to canvas** is on in the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/). A screen smaller than the canvas isn't scaled up.
38	
39	### Corner
40	
41	The camera shows its whole picture, with square corners, in the corner you choose. It's fitted inside a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third tall, 5 % in from the canvas's edges. This is the box a recording's camera lands in by default.
42	
43	### Rounded Corner
44	
45	The same box with rounded corners, the radius 8 % of the box's shorter side.
46	
47	### Circle
48	
49	The largest square of the camera's picture, cropped to a circle in the corner you choose. The circle is as wide as the box's shorter side, so on a 16:9 canvas it's a third of the canvas's height, and it sits 5 % in from the edges.
50	
51	### Side by Side
52	
53	The screen is fitted in the left two-thirds and the camera is cropped to fill the right third. There's a margin of 4 % of the canvas's shorter side around and between them, and both have their corners rounded by 2 % of that side. It needs a screen.
54	
55	### Stacked
56	
57	The screen runs across the top, centred, and takes up to two-thirds of the height inside the margins. The camera is cropped to fill the rest below it. The margins and corners are the same as Side by Side's. It needs a screen, and it works on any canvas, not only a tall one.
58	
59	### Camera Full
60	
61	The camera fills the canvas, with square corners. It's scaled until no canvas shows, so a picture of another shape runs off two edges.
62	
63	### Screen Only
64	
65	The camera is hidden where it is, its opacity going to 0, and the screen goes to its full placement. The camera clip keeps playing, so its sound carries on.
66	
67	## Which clips
68	
69	Frame Job works out the camera and the screen from the selection and the playhead. They don't have to come from a recording: any clip with a picture can be the camera, and any clip with a picture behind it can be the screen.
70	
71	| Selected | The camera | The screen |
72	| --- | --- | --- |
73	| Two clips with a picture, on different tracks | The front one | The other one |
74	| One clip with a picture | That clip | The clip drawing behind it at the playhead |
75	| Nothing | The clip at the playhead on the front-most track named "Camera" | The clip drawing behind it at the playhead |
76	
77	The clip drawing behind the camera is the front-most one playing at the playhead on a track behind the camera's. Frame Job passes over hidden tracks, [matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/), [adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) and clips with their picture switched off.
78	
79	With no screen, the corner layouts, Camera Full and Screen Only lay out the camera alone. Side by Side and Stacked won't.
80	
81	The items are dimmed when:
82	
83	- the camera doesn't play at the playhead. A selected clip the playhead isn't on doesn't fall back to the "Camera" track
84	- three or more clips are selected, or two on one track
85	- a selected clip has no picture of its own, such as a text clip, an adjustment clip or a sound-only clip
86	- a sheet is open
87	
88	The menu works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/). There, the nest's canvas is the canvas and the "Camera" track is the one inside the nest.
89	
90	## The switch
91	
92	A switch eases from the old layout into the new one over 0.5 s from the playhead. It's a layout action on each clip, so you can see it on the clip's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) and retime it like any other action. Each action sets position, scale, crop, corner radius and opacity.
93	
94	- **At a clip's first frame** it cuts instead of easing. The layout becomes the clip's own placement there, and a one-frame action marks the cut. Each clip is judged on its own, so a camera that starts at the playhead cuts while the screen behind it eases.
95	- **Near an end** the switch is shortened to finish by the clip's end or the clip's next layout action, and it's never shorter than one frame.
96	- **While another layout is still easing,** the first one ends where the second begins.
97	- **Where a layout action already starts,** the new layout replaces it.
98	
99	## How far a layout reaches
100	
101	A layout holds until the next switch, so a camera cut into pieces stays in the corner.
102	
103	Every later clip with a picture on the camera's track, and on the screen's, that starts before the next layout action on that track takes the layout as its own placement, with no easing. With no later switch, that runs to the end of the track. Each track's reach is worked out separately.
104	
105	Those later clips keep their own actions, though an action that moves one can [stop the switch](/framing/layout-section/#a-layout-meets-a-zoom). Because a later clip takes the layout as its placement, removing the layout action afterwards doesn't put that clip back. Use Undo for that.
106	
107	## When a switch is refused
108	
109	A switch that can't be made changes nothing. Frame Job beeps, and [the foot of the inspector](/getting-started/refused-edits/#the-refusal-strip) shows the reason after "Refused:". The numbers in it are Frame Job's own ids for the clip and the action, and the timecode is when that clip starts or, in the first two rows, the playhead.
110	
111	| The inspector says | What it means |
112	| --- | --- |
113	| "clip 12 does not play at 00:00:04:10" | The clip isn't under the playhead. Move the playhead onto it. With two clips selected, this can be the screen. |
114	| "no clip draws behind clip 12 at 00:00:04:10 to be the screen" | Side by Side or Stacked found no screen. Pick another layout, or put a clip behind the camera. |
115	| "clip 12 is a nest clip, which cannot draw a rounded corner or a circle." | A nest clip shows square corners only, so a nest can't take Rounded Corner or Circle as the camera. That goes for a later camera clip in the layout's reach too. Use Corner. |
116	| "The screen clip 8 at 00:00:00:00 zooms (action 10); nest the screen's clips…" | The clip holds a zoom or another moving action after the playhead. See [A layout meets a zoom](/framing/layout-section/#a-layout-meets-a-zoom), which also covers the sheet Frame Job usually offers here. |
117	| "action 10 on clip 8 already runs from …, and two actions on one clip may not overlap" | Two actions on one clip can't overlap, and the switch's span runs into another action, such as a volume change. Move the playhead, shorten the switch in the [Layout section](/framing/layout-section/), or move that action. |
118	
119	## Good to know
120	
121	- A layout sets position, scale, crop, corner radius and opacity on both clips, replacing what you'd set by hand. Rotation and everything else stay as they were.
122	- A nest clip in Side by Side or Stacked keeps square corners.
123	- Side by Side stays side by side on a tall canvas if you choose it there. [Make Vertical Version](/framing/vertical-what-changes/) is what re-lays your switches for a new shape, and it turns Side by Side into Stacked on a canvas taller than wide.
124	- The camera's crop in Circle, Side by Side and Stacked can [centre on the person](/framing/layout-section/#the-crop-centred-on-the-person) instead of the picture.
125	
126	## With an agent
127	
128	`switch_layout` does what the menu does, at any time rather than the playhead. An agent can also:
129	
130	- name the camera and the screen itself. The screen must be on a track behind the camera's, and each must have a picture and play at that time
131	- set how long the switch takes and how it eases, where the menu always eases in and out over 0.5 s
132	- stop a layout holding at a time of its choosing, with no later switch
133	- switch inside a nest without opening it, where that nest's canvas is the canvas. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/)
134	
135	See [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/). An agent can also choose a recording's layout when it [records](/mcp/record-screen/).
136

2	title: Follow the speaker in a vertical
3	description: Make a vertical version of a wide interview that cuts to whoever is talking, using a microphone per person.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A wide shot of two to four people doesn't fit a tall frame. Follow Speaker solves that: in [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/), it reads each person's microphone and cuts the frame to whoever is talking.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
13	  where="Follow ▸ Speaker in the sheet"
14	  tools={['make_vertical_version', 'reframe_clip']}
15	  needs="A microphone for each person, on its own track. Faces are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
16	/>
17	
18	## What you need
19	
20	- A wide shot: a full-frame movie clip with the people in it.
21	- A sound file for each person, from a recorder or a lavalier rather than a camera, each on its own track and recorded with the shot.
22	- Those sound files lined up with the shot. Use [**Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**](/audio/synchronize-audio/) first.
23	
24	## Follow the speaker
25	
26	<Steps>
27	
28	1. Choose **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** and set **Follow** to **Speaker**. The **Microphones** and **Faces** rows appear.
29	
30	2. Under [**Microphones**](#microphones), tick the tracks that belong to the people in the shot, two to four.
31	
32	3. Under [**Faces**](#faces), check that each row names that microphone's person. If the movies haven't been analysed yet the pop-ups have no faces for now.
33	
34	4. Choose **Make**. If an analysis has to run first, [the sheet comes back](#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis) when it's done, so you can do step 3 and choose **Make** there.
35	
36	</Steps>
37	
38	The other controls work as they do in [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/#the-controls).
39	
40	## Microphones
41	
42	A checkbox for each track holding a sound file, named by the track and listed front to back. Sound from a movie file doesn't count, so a camera's track isn't offered, and neither is a track whose clips all have their sound off. The first four are ticked.
43	
44	Tick the ones that belong to the people in the shot. **Make** needs two to four, so with more than four tracks listed, check which four are ticked.
45	
46	When no full-frame movie plays beside two ticked microphones, the sheet says "No full-frame movie clip plays beside two of the ticked microphones, so nobody can be framed by who is talking." and **Make** stays dimmed. Check that the shot and the microphones overlap on the timeline.
47	
48	## Faces
49	
50	One row per ticked microphone, with a pop-up of the faces Frame Job found in the longest shot it can frame this way. Faces are numbered left to right, with where each sits across the picture: **Face 1 (42 % across)**.
51	
52	Ticking or unticking a microphone rebuilds the rows and offers the match again for the new set. Otherwise your own choice stands.
53	
54	### The automatic match
55	
56	Frame Job matches each microphone to the face whose mouth moves while it talks. When the match is clear the pop-ups are already set, and the note under them reads "Each microphone is matched to the face that talks with it; change one if it is wrong." Check that each row names that microphone's person.
57	
58	A match is clear when every microphone agrees with its face to at least 0.2, on a scale where 1 is perfect agreement and 0 is none. A face is counted when it's in at least a quarter of the shot, and four faces at most are considered.
59	
60	### Choose a face
61	
62	When the match isn't clear, each pop-up says **Choose a face** and the note reads "The faces do not show clearly who is on each microphone: choose each microphone's face." Pick each microphone's face yourself.
63	
64	If the shot shows fewer faces than the ticked microphones under it, the pop-ups have no faces to offer. Untick the microphones of people who aren't in it.
65	
66	## When Make is offered
67	
68	**Make** is available when all of these are true:
69	
70	- Two to four microphones are ticked.
71	- A full-frame movie plays at the same time as at least two of them.
72	- Every ticked microphone has a face of its own. Two microphones can't share a face.
73	
74	While an analysis is still to be made there are no faces to choose yet, so the last rule waits: **Make** is available with the first two, and choosing it runs the analysis.
75	
76	A microphone imported moments ago may still be being measured. The sheet says so in the words [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) uses, such as "The microphone on track 3 is still being analysed — its loudness has not been measured yet. Try again in a moment." Choose the command again in a moment. A microphone with no speech under the shot stops **Make** in the same way, with "The microphone on track 3 has no speech between …". Untick it.
77	
78	## The sheet comes back after analysis
79	
80	The summary warns you first: "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 3 files on this Mac first, then asks you to confirm who is on each microphone, then makes a 1080 × 1920 version."
81	
82	When you choose **Make**, the Analyzing sheet runs. Then the sheet comes back on the same shape, **Follow**, **Zoom**, **Where Empty**, **Make a copy** and ticked microphones, this time with faces to confirm. Nothing is made until you choose **Make** there. **Stop** on the Analyzing sheet makes nothing.
83	
84	## How the shot is cut
85	
86	A shot is framed this way when it's a full-frame movie, its file is present, it has no cursor file, it isn't on a microphone track, and it overlaps sound on at least two ticked microphones. Frame Job doesn't count the people in it. The summary counts these shots: "Follows whoever is talking in 1 clip."
87	
88	Who talks when is read the way Switch by Speaker reads the microphones, with its default settings, so the two agree.
89	
90	- Each change of speaker is a cut, not a move.
91	- Each framing holds at least 2 s, so a short reply doesn't cut away and back.
92	- Two people talking at once are framed together when they fit. When they don't, the frame stays on the person already in it.
93	- While nobody talks, the last speaker stays.
94	
95	Every other movie clip follows its faces, and screen recordings and everything else are treated as usual. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).
96	
97	## Shots that follow their faces instead
98	
99	A shot that can't be framed by who is talking follows its faces instead, and the summary says why: "Clip 3 is followed, but it follows its faces, not who is talking, because …". The reasons include:
100	
101	- It changes shot. Follow Speaker frames one wide shot, so split the clip first with **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**.
102	- It shows fewer faces than the microphones under it.
103	- Nobody talks inside it on those microphones.
104	
105	## Good to know
106	
107	- The faces you confirm come from the longest shot and apply to every shot by number, counting left to right. If people sit in a different order in another shot, that shot frames the wrong person.
108	- A shot uses only the ticked microphones that sound under it, so a microphone used elsewhere in the timeline doesn't count against it.
109	- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) doesn't offer **Speaker**. Only Make Vertical Version and an agent do.
110	
111	## With an agent
112	
113	An agent makes the same version with `make_vertical_version`, naming two to four microphone clips, each standing for its track, and the faces if it wants to set them. Nobody confirms a match, so a shot whose faces don't show who is whose follows its faces unless the call names them, and the agent is told why. It's also told which microphones and faces each shot used. `reframe_clip` frames one clip on whoever is talking, on the canvas it's already on. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
114

118	- [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)
119	- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/)

3	description: "Frame the selected movie clips on the person or thing in them, with eased moves you can edit and a blurred copy behind where the whole picture shows."
4	---

7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Follow Subject keeps the person in shot when a clip's picture doesn't fit the canvas, such as a landscape recording on a 1080 × 1920 vertical canvas. It finds the subject, moves the frame with it, and writes each move as an ordinary action you can change.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Clip ▸ Follow Subject…"
14	  where="Each move, on the clip's action lane"
15	  tools="reframe_clip"
16	  needs="Nothing. Faces, people and shot changes are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
17	/>
18	
19	## Frame clips on their subject
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Set the canvas you want first, in the [Document tab](/projects/canvas-size/). Follow Subject doesn't change the canvas.
24	
25	2. Select the clips to frame.
26	
27	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**. It's available when a selected clip plays a movie and no sheet is open, inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) too. There's no keyboard shortcut.
28	
29	4. Set [Follow](#follow), [Zoom](#zoom) and [Where Empty](#where-empty).
30	
31	5. Read [the summary](#the-summary) under the controls, which says what will happen.
32	
33	6. Choose **Follow** (<kbd>Return</kbd>), or **Cancel** (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) to leave everything as it was.
34	
35	</Steps>
36	
37	<Shot
38	  name="15i-follow-subject-sheet.sheet"
39	  alt="The Follow Subject sheet, with Follow set to Subject, Zoom at 125 percent and Where Empty set to Show Whole. A summary reads: Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 1 file on this Mac first, then frames 1 clip. Cancel and Follow buttons sit at the bottom right."
40	/>
41	
42	:::tip
43	To change the canvas and frame a whole timeline in one go, use [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) instead.
44	:::
45	
46	A still, a picture, a nest, text, a shape, a graphic or an adjustment clip in the selection is left alone, with no line in the summary.
47	
48	## The controls
49	
50	### Follow
51	
52	Follow chooses what the frame stays on.
53	
54	| Choice | What the frame follows |
55	| --- | --- |
56	| **Subject** | A face, or where there's none a person, or where there's neither the region the eye goes to. This is the default. |
57	| **Faces** | Faces only |
58	| **People** | People only |
59	| **Salient Region** | Salient regions only |
60	| **Center** | Nothing. The frame holds on the middle of the picture for the whole clip, with no analysis needed. |
61	
62	### Zoom
63	
64	Zoom sets how tight the frame is, in whole percents from 100 to 400. A value outside that range is brought back to it when you leave the field. At 100 % the picture is the smallest it can be and still cover the canvas.
65	
66	It starts at 100 %. If the first selected clip's picture is within 1 % of the canvas's shape, it starts at 125 % instead, because at 100 % such a picture fills the canvas exactly and the frame has no room to move.
67	
68	Zoom enlarges the picture, and so does putting a landscape picture on a tall canvas. A 1080p source on a 1080 × 1920 canvas is already enlarged ×1.78 at 100 %.
69	
70	### Where Empty
71	
72	Where Empty sets what the frame shows while there's nothing to follow.
73	
74	| Choice | What shows |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| **Show Whole** | The whole picture, with a [blurred copy](#the-blurred-backgrounds-track) filling the canvas around it. This is the default. |
77	| **Center** | The middle of the picture, at the same zoom |
78	
79	It's dimmed while Follow is **Center**.
80	
81	### What's remembered
82	
83	**Follow** and **Where Empty** are remembered for next time, and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) shares them. They're saved when you choose **Follow**, even if you then stop the analysis, and never on **Cancel**. If Make Vertical Version last used **Speaker**, which this sheet doesn't offer, Follow opens on **Subject**. **Zoom** isn't remembered.
84	
85	## The summary
86	
87	Under the controls, the sheet says what **Follow** will do. It updates as you change a control, and after you leave the Zoom field.
88	
89	| The sheet says | What it means |
90	| --- | --- |
91	| "Frames 2 clips." | How many clips will change. |
92	| "Adds a Backgrounds track for the blurred copy." | Some of the framing shows the whole picture, so a [blurred copy](#the-blurred-backgrounds-track) goes behind it. |
93	| "Adds 1 more track behind it where clips overlap." | Two selected clips overlap in time, so their copies need separate tracks. |
94	| "2 actions re-eased at a cut." | A shot change landed inside actions the clip already had, and each was split there and eased again on either side. See [It starts from the whole picture](#it-starts-from-the-whole-picture). |
95	| "1 action carries a framing move." | A move couldn't fit between the clip's own actions, so one of them carries it. |
96	| "Clip 3 is already framed this way." | That clip wouldn't change. |
97	| "Clip 3: …" | That clip can't be framed, and this is why. See [Clips it cannot frame](#clips-it-cannot-frame). |
98	| "Reading the analysis…" | Frame Job is loading what it found earlier. **Follow** is dimmed until it's done. |
99	| "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 1 file on this Mac first, then frames 1 clip." | The [analysis comes first](#analysis-first). |
100	
101	**Follow** is dimmed when nothing would change.
102	
103	"Clip 3" uses Frame Job's own number for the clip, which isn't its position on the timeline.
104	
105	## Analysis first
106	
107	When the clips haven't been analysed, choosing **Follow** closes the sheet and opens the [Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) while Frame Job finds what it needs on your Mac. It then frames the clips by itself.
108	
109	The Analyzing sheet has a row for each file and each kind of analysis still to be made: **Shot changes**, **Faces**, and **People and salient regions**. Only the part of each file the clip plays is read, plus a second either side.
110	
111	**Stop** changes nothing. **Center** needs no analysis, so it frames at once.
112	
113	Frame Job beeps and frames nothing in these cases, and says why at the foot of the inspector, after **Refused:**
114	
115	| The inspector says | What happened |
116	| --- | --- |
117	| "the project changed while Follow Subject was analyzing, so nothing was framed. Choose Follow Subject again." | The project changed, or you went into or out of a nest, while the analysis ran. What was found is kept, so a second try doesn't start over. |
118	| "The faces analysis of “interview.mov” failed: …" | An analysis couldn't finish. The sentence names the kind and the file. |
119	
120	## It starts from the whole picture
121	
122	Each clip is framed from the whole picture. Its own positions and scales are replaced, both the clip's base values and any an action sets. An action left with nothing to do is removed. The clip's volume and its other actions stay, and so does its crop, which the frame stays inside.
123	
124	The moves then fit around the actions that remain:
125	
126	- A move goes in a gap between them.
127	- A move that would overlap an action starts up to 0.5 s earlier to clear it.
128	- A move that still can't clear is carried by the action it overlaps, along that action's curve.
129	- A shot change that lands inside an action splits it into three: the part before, the one frame of the cut, and the part after. A steady (linear) action plays as it did, and an eased one is eased again on each side.
130	- A speed action, or an action a trim left running past the clip's end, is never cut. It carries the change instead.
131	
132	## How following moves
133	
134	While it follows, the frame stays inside the picture, so nothing past the picture's edge shows.
135	
136	### Which subject it follows
137	
138	When several faces or people are in view, Frame Job scores each on how steadily it's there, how big it is and how central it is, over the second either side and within the shot.
139	
140	It stays with its choice. Another subject takes over only after scoring at least 25 % better for 2 s, so two similar faces don't trade the frame back and forth. With **Subject**, a person's body stands in for their face while the face can't be found.
141	
142	Frame Job samples the picture ten times a second, and only the first eight of each kind in a sample count. For faces, that's the eight furthest left.
143	
144	### Where the subject sits
145	
146	| Subject | Where it sits |
147	| --- | --- |
148	| A face | In the middle of the frame, or 38 % of the way down on a frame taller than wide, leaving room below for the rest of the person |
149	| A person | With the top of their box 12 % of the way down the frame |
150	| A salient region | In the middle of the frame |
151	
152	This is where the frame aims. Near the picture's edge it stops at the edge, so the subject sits off from these marks.
153	
154	### Easing and staying put
155	
156	The frame eases onto the subject and moves only when the subject leaves the middle of the frame, so a speaker who sways stays put. The middle counts as 15 % of the frame's width and 12 % of its height either side.
157	
158	A move travels at 0.8 frame widths a second and takes at least 0.4 s. No move starts within 0.5 s of the last one's end, unless the subject has left the frame altogether.
159	
160	### At a shot change
161	
162	The frame cuts with the picture, landing on the first frame of the new shot. It's placed on where the subject sits over the new shot's first second. No move runs across a cut.
163	
164	### When the subject is lost
165	
166	The frame holds for a second, so a blink or a turned head changes nothing. It then follows someone else in the shot if there's anyone. If not, it eases over 0.8 s to your [Where Empty](#where-empty) choice.
167	
168	It comes back once a subject has been in view for 0.6 s.
169	
170	A clip with nobody in view during its first second opens on Where Empty. A clip with nothing to follow at all stays on Where Empty for its whole length.
171	
172	### Two people
173	
174	The frame holds two faces or two people together when both fit in it. Each box is widened by 15 % before they're tested against the frame. Salient regions aren't paired.
175	
176	## The blurred Backgrounds track
177	
178	Where the frame shows the whole picture, the canvas shows around it. So a blurred copy of the clip goes on a new track named **Backgrounds** at the back, for the clip's whole length. That's the same copy [**Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/#blurred-background) makes: picture only, filling the canvas.
179	
180	No track is added when no clip needs one. That's always so when Follow or Where Empty is **Center**. Where two selected clips overlap in time, the second copy goes on a further new track behind Backgrounds.
181	
182	A clip with speed actions keeps them on its copy, so the copy shows the same frames.
183	
184	## Every move is an action
185	
186	Every move is an ordinary action on the clip's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/). To nudge where a frame ends, select the action and [drag the picture on the canvas](/motion/edit-an-action/#edit-on-the-canvas). You can [move, resize or remove it](/motion/change-an-action/) as you would any other.
187	
188	## Undo
189	
190	**Edit ▸ Undo Follow Subject** takes the whole command back in one step, every clip and track included. What was found stays in the cache.
191	
192	## Screen recordings are skipped
193	
194	A screen recording Frame Job made, with its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), isn't followed by faces. Follow Subject leaves it unanalysed and lists it under the summary:
195	
196	> Clip 3: clip 3's media has a cursor file, so it follows the cursor, not faces; frame it with cursor, center, fit or keep
197	
198	Of those, the sheet offers **Center**. [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) follows the pointer instead, and an agent can [follow it too](/framing/reframe-clip/).
199	
200	## Clips it cannot frame
201	
202	A selected movie clip that can't be followed gets a line under the summary, and the others are still framed. With no clip left to frame, the summary shows only those lines and **Follow** stays dimmed.
203	
204	| Clip | The line says | What you can do |
205	| --- | --- | --- |
206	| On a matte track | "clip 3 is on a matte track, which framing would move; only keep reframes it" | Change the track's [matte setting](/canvas/matte-tracks/) or move the clip |
207	| Cut by a matte | "clip 3 is cut by the matte on track 7, which framing would move it out of; only keep reframes it" | The same |
208	| Rotated | "clip 3 is turned 15°, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | Set its [rotation](/canvas/transform/) back to 0° |
209	| Turned by an action | "clip 3's action 12 turns it, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | Take rotation out of [that action](/motion/edit-an-action/#take-a-property-out-of-the-action) |
210	| Spinning | "clip 3 spins in its motion, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | [Clear the spin preset](/motion/motion-presets/#change-or-clear-a-preset) |
211	| Cropped or scaled to nothing | "clip 3's crop or scale leaves no picture to frame" | Fix its [crop](/canvas/crop/) or scale |
212	| With a cursor file | See [above](#screen-recordings-are-skipped) | Choose **Center** |
213	| With no analysis under it | "clip 3 has no subjects to follow; analyze it first" | Lengthen the clip. Frame Job samples a file ten times a second, so a very short clip can fall between two samples. |
214	
215	"keep" and the other lowercase words in these lines are an agent's options. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/).
216	
217	A clip with nobody in it isn't one of these. It's framed on your [Where Empty](#where-empty) choice.
218	
219	When an analysis has to run first, the sheet can't list these lines yet. Afterwards the clips that can be framed are framed, and the rest stay as they were with no message. If none can be, Frame Job beeps and shows the lines at the foot of the inspector.
220	
221	## Good to know
222	
223	- If a selected clip's file is missing or can't be read, the summary says so and **Follow** stays dimmed for all of them. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/), or choose **Center**, which doesn't read the file.
224	- Follow Subject doesn't frame stills or pictures. [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) can centre them.
225	- Running Follow Subject again on a clip whose frame shows the whole picture adds another Backgrounds track and another copy, and the first copy stays. Undo the first run, or delete the old copy.
226	- Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the nest's canvas is the canvas, and the Backgrounds track goes in the nest.
227	- A clip's speed, speed ramps and reversal are all taken into account, so the frame moves with what the clip shows.
228	
229	## With an agent
230	
231	`reframe_clip` frames one clip at a time. Follow Subject is that tool run on each selected clip, starting from the whole picture, with a Backgrounds track behind. The sheet's **Where Empty** is the tool's `where_empty`: `fit` for **Show Whole**, which is the default, or `center`.
232	
233	An agent has more choices than the sheet. It can show the whole picture, rescale a clip from the canvas it was made for, follow a recorded pointer or follow whoever's talking, and it can compose the framing into a clip's own moves instead of replacing them. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).

10	The Layout section is the inspector's way to make a [camera layout](/framing/camera-layouts/) switch. It lays out the selected clip as the camera and, unlike the menu, lets you choose how long the switch takes.
11	
12	<AtAGlance

14	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Layout"
15	  tools="switch_layout"
16	  needs="Nothing for a layout. A crop centres on the person only when Remove Background has already made the camera's masks, on your Mac."

19	<Shot
20	  name="05j-clip-layout.inspector"
21	  alt="The Picture sub-tab scrolled to the open Layout section, its summary reading Square, Bottom Right. Layout is set to Corner, Shape to Square, Corner to Bottom Right and Duration to 0.50 s, with the Switch at Playhead button underneath."

23	
24	## Switch at Playhead
25	
26	<Steps>
27	
28	1. Select the camera clip, and only that clip. It needs to be a clip of a video file with a picture. An image, a still or a nest gets no Layout section, though [the menu](/framing/camera-layouts/#which-clips) can lay one out.
29	
30	2. Open **Layout** in the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab. It comes after Transform and Behind Subject, and it's shut until you open it.
31	
32	3. Set the [controls](#the-controls).
33	
34	4. Move the playhead onto the clip, to where the switch should start.
35	
36	5. Press **Switch at Playhead**.
37	
38	</Steps>
39	
40	This does exactly what **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸** does, with this clip as the camera and the clip drawing behind it as the screen. It's one undo step, **Camera Layout**. Everything in [The switch](/framing/camera-layouts/#the-switch) and [How far a layout reaches](/framing/camera-layouts/#how-far-a-layout-reaches) applies.
41	
42	The button is off while a sheet is open. Pressed with the playhead off the clip, the foot of the inspector says the clip doesn't play there and nothing changes.
43	
44	## The controls
45	
46	| Control | What it does | Default | Choices |
47	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
48	| **Layout** | The layout to switch to. | Corner | Corner, Side by Side, Stacked, Camera Full, Screen Only |
49	| **Shape** | The corner picture's shape. Square is the menu's **Corner ▸**, Rounded its **Rounded Corner ▸**. Greyed for any layout but Corner. | Square | Square, Rounded, Circle |
50	| **Corner** | Which canvas corner the camera sits in. Greyed for any layout but Corner. | Bottom Right | Bottom Right, Bottom Left, Top Right, Top Left |
51	| **Duration** | How long the switch takes. | 0.5 s | 0.01 to 10 s |
52	
53	The section's header sums up what it would switch to: "Square, Bottom Right", or "Side by Side".
54	
55	Type a **Duration**, or pick 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 from the arrow in the field. A typed number outside the range goes to the nearest end of it. The switch is then rounded to whole frames, and a length under half a frame rounds to nothing, so Frame Job shows an error and doesn't switch. That's 0.01 s on a 30 fps project. At a clip's first frame the switch cuts, whatever the Duration.
56	
57	These choices belong to the section, not to the project. They stay while the window is open, they aren't saved and they aren't undo steps, so nothing changes until you press **Switch at Playhead**. There's no Reset.
58	
59	## The crop centred on the person
60	
61	Circle, Side by Side and Stacked crop the camera. When the camera's person masks already exist for every frame the clip plays, the crop centres on the person, at the middle of where the masks find them, averaged over the clip. This works from the menu and the section alike.
62	
63	[Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) makes the masks, on your Mac, and they stay in the project's cache. You can turn Remove Background off again afterwards. A layout never starts that analysis itself. With no masks, or masks for only part of the clip, the crop centres on the picture. A camera that's an image clip centres on the picture, masks or not.
64	
65	Frame Job reads the masks for a moment before it switches. If the project changes in that moment, it beeps and makes no switch. Choose the layout again.
66	
67	## A layout meets a zoom
68	
69	A switch never fights a zoom. Frame Job won't switch when a clip it would move holds a zoom or another moving action after the playhead, because the two would pull the clip in different directions.
70	
71	A moving action is any action that changes position, scale, crop, corner radius or opacity, other than a layout action. On the clip under the playhead, only an action that ends after the playhead counts, so moving the playhead past the end of a zoom clears the way. On a later clip in the layout's [reach](/framing/camera-layouts/#how-far-a-layout-reaches), any moving action counts.
72	
73	There's one exception. In Corner, Camera Full and Screen Only, a screen still at its [full placement](/framing/camera-layouts/#the-layouts) stays where it is, so its zooms keep playing and the switch goes ahead. Side by Side and Stacked always move the screen.
74	
75	When a nest would let the switch go ahead, Frame Job offers one. Otherwise the foot of the inspector names the clip and the action, and nothing changes. To make the switch anyway, move the playhead past the end of that action if it's on the clip under the playhead, or [remove the action](/motion/change-an-action/#remove-an-action), then switch again.
76	
77	## Lay out the clips in a nest?
78	
79	This sheet shows the reason the switch couldn't be made, then offers to put those clips in a [nest](/editing/nests/) first. The layout then moves the nest, and the zoom keeps playing inside it.
80	
81	- **Nest and Switch** makes the nest and the layout. One undo step, **Camera Layout**, takes both back.
82	- **Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> changes nothing.
83	
84	What goes in the nest is the clip at the playhead and the later clips in the layout's reach, apart from a clip that holds the next switch. Only the side that stopped the switch is nested, so a screen that zooms is nested and its camera isn't. If both the camera and the screen hold a moving action, each gets a nest of its own.
85	
86	There's no offer when:
87	
88	- one of those clips is already laid out, because a nest would lay it out twice. That includes a clip that sits anywhere but its [full placement](/framing/camera-layouts/#the-layouts), such as a camera a recording landed in the corner
89	- the camera holds the moving action and you chose Rounded Corner or Circle, because a nest clip shows square corners only
90	
91	When the camera itself goes into a nest, its crop centres on the nest's picture rather than the person.
92	
93	## With an agent
94	
95	An agent is never shown the sheet. It asks for the nest in the same `switch_layout` call, and Frame Job won't do that when one of the clips is already laid out.
96	
97	An agent can also centre the camera's crop on a point of its own choosing, and that point stays as sent even when the camera goes into a nest. If it doesn't choose one, the crop is filled from the masks as it is for the menu, and the call's answer gives the centre it used. See [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
98

2	title: Make Vertical Version
3	description: Turn a landscape edit into a tall or square version for a phone, a reel or a square post, in one step over the whole timeline.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Make Vertical Version makes a tall or square version of a landscape edit, for a phone, a reel or a square post. It changes the canvas and reworks the whole timeline in one step, so you don't have to frame each clip yourself.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
14	  tools="make_vertical_version"
15	  needs="Nothing. Faces, people and shot changes are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
16	/>
17	
18	## Make a vertical version
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Choose **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**. It has no keyboard shortcut. It's available when the project has a clip, no [nest](/editing/nests/) is open, no other sheet is up and nothing is recording.
23	
24	2. Pick a [**Shape**](#shape).
25	
26	3. Choose what to [**Follow**](#follow), and set [**Zoom**](#zoom) and [**Where Empty**](#where-empty) if you want to.
27	
28	4. Leave [**Make a copy**](#make-a-copy) ticked to keep this project as it is, or untick it to change this project.
29	
30	5. [Read the summary](#read-the-summary) under the controls. It says what will happen before anything does.
31	
32	6. Choose **Make** (<kbd>Return</kbd>), or **Cancel** (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) to leave everything as it was.
33	
34	</Steps>
35	
36	<Shot
37	  name="15j-make-vertical-sheet.sheet"
38	  alt="The Make Vertical Version sheet, with Shape on 9:16 (540 × 960), Follow on Subject, Zoom at 100 %, Where Empty on Show Whole and Make a copy ticked. The summary under them reads: Makes a 540 × 960 version. Keeps 4 clips as placed."
39	/>
40	
41	Each clip is treated by what it is: full-frame movies follow their subject, screen recordings follow the pointer, camera layouts are laid out again, and so on. [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/) goes through it clip by clip.
42	
43	## The controls
44	
45	### Shape
46	
47	Each row shows the size it makes, such as **9:16 (1080 × 1920)**. The new canvas keeps the old short side, rounded down to an even number, and the height follows from the shape.
48	
49	| Shape | From 1920 × 1080 |
50	| --- | --- |
51	| **9:16** | 1080 × 1920 |
52	| **4:5** | 1080 × 1350 |
53	| **1:1** | 1080 × 1080 |
54	
55	A shape the canvas already has isn't in the list.
56	
57	### Follow
58	
59	What each movie clip keeps in the frame.
60	
61	| Choice | What the frame follows |
62	| --- | --- |
63	| **Subject** | A face. Where there's no face, a person. Where there's neither, the region the eye goes to. |
64	| **Faces** | Faces only. |
65	| **People** | People only. |
66	| **Salient Region** | Only the region the eye goes to. |
67	| **Speaker** | Whoever is talking, for a wide shot with a microphone per person. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/). |
68	| **Center** | The middle of the picture, for the whole clip. Needs no analysis, so the summary is ready at once. |
69	
70	These are the choices of [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/), plus **Speaker**. The two commands share one remembered choice, saved when you choose **Make**. It starts on **Subject**. If you last chose **Speaker**, Follow Subject, which doesn't offer it, opens on **Subject**.
71	
72	### Zoom
73	
74	How tight the frame is, from 100 to 400 %, in whole numbers. 100 % is the smallest scale at which a picture covers the new canvas. Higher values frame closer.
75	
76	**Zoom** starts at 100 % each time you choose the command and isn't remembered. The one exception is the sheet that [comes back after a Speaker analysis](/framing/follow-speaker/#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis), which keeps what you set. The summary updates when you leave the field.
77	
78	### Where Empty
79	
80	What a followed clip shows while there's nothing to follow.
81	
82	| Choice | What the frame shows |
83	| --- | --- |
84	| **Show Whole** | The whole picture on a blurred copy of itself. This is the default. |
85	| **Center** | The middle of the picture. |
86	
87	It's dimmed while **Follow** is **Center**. It's the same remembered choice as Follow Subject's.
88	
89	### Make a copy
90	
91	Ticked, the vertical version opens as a new untitled project and this project doesn't change. The copy is named after this project with the shape, such as "Interview (9:16)", "Interview (4:5)" or "Interview (1:1)". It carries the project's caches and analysis. Save it when you want to keep it.
92	
93	Unticked, this project itself becomes the vertical version.
94	
95	The box is ticked each time you choose the command, and your choice isn't remembered. Only the sheet that comes back after a Speaker analysis keeps what you chose.
96	
97	## Read the summary
98	
99	Under the controls, the sheet says what **Make** will do, and it changes as you change a control. It opens with the new size, "Makes a 1080 × 1920 version.", and goes on with whichever of these apply:
100	
101	| The summary says | What it means |
102	| --- | --- |
103	| "Follows 3 clips." | Movie clips that follow what you chose. |
104	| "Follows the cursor in 2 clips, their own zooms and pans replaced." | Screen recordings that follow the pointer. |
105	| "Follows whoever is talking in 1 clip." | Wide shots framed on the speaker. |
106	| "Re-lays 2 camera layouts for the new canvas." | Camera layout switches made again. |
107	| "Shows 1 clip whole on a blurred copy." | Clips with nothing to follow at any point. |
108	| "Keeps 4 clips as placed." | Clips moved and scaled to the new canvas, not framed. |
109	| "Re-fills 1 background." | Blurred copies and background plates resized to cover the new canvas. |
110	| "Removes 1 blurred copy the framing replaces." | Old blurred copies that are no longer needed. |
111	| "Re-sizes 1 graphic to the new canvas." | Graphics exactly the old canvas's size. |
112	| "Updates 1 graphic module to the current template." | Older copies of a bundled template, in a copy only. |
113	| "Adds a Backgrounds track for the blurred copy." | A new track at the back for the blurred copies. |
114	| "Adds 1 more track behind it where clips overlap." | A further track, for copies that overlap in time. |
115	| "2 actions re-eased at a cut." | A shot change landed inside actions a clip already had, so each was split there and eased again on either side. |
116	| "2 actions carry a framing move." | A framing move couldn't fit between a clip's own actions, so those actions carry it. |
117	| "Re-lays 1 caption track for the new canvas." | Word captions paged again for the narrow frame. |
118	
119	After those come single lines for what needs your attention:
120	
121	- One line per camera layout switch: "Re-laid: Side by Side → Stacked at 00:00:10:00."
122	- One line per clip that isn't followed, or is only partly followed, with the reason: "Clip 6 is not followed: its media file is missing, so it is kept as placed." or "Clip 2 is followed, but it is shown whole on a blurred copy where no subject is found."
123	- One line per caption track that's kept as it was, and one per graphic module left as it is.
124	
125	If the movies have already been analysed, the summary reads "Reading the analysis…" for a moment, and **Make** is dimmed until it's done.
126	
127	If Frame Job can't make the new version, the summary says why and **Make** stays dimmed. When an analysis has to run first, Frame Job beeps after it instead and says why at the foot of the inspector. A project at its limit of 64 tracks, nests included, is one such case, because Make Vertical needs a track for the blurred copies.
128	
129	## When the movies need analysing
130	
131	Following a subject needs to know where the faces, people and shot changes are. When the movies haven't been analysed yet, the summary says so: "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 3 files on this Mac first, then makes a 1080 × 1920 version."
132	
133	**Make** then shows the Analyzing sheet while that runs on your Mac, and makes the version when it's done. **Stop** makes nothing: no project opens and this one doesn't change.
134	
135	**Center** needs no analysis, and a recording that follows its pointer is never analysed. With **Speaker**, the sheet comes back after the analysis so you can [confirm who is on each microphone](/framing/follow-speaker/#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis).
136	
137	If an analysis fails, Frame Job beeps, makes nothing and names the file at the foot of the inspector.
138	
139	## Make another shape
140	
141	What was found stays in this project's cache and is carried into the copy, so making another shape afterwards needs no analysis. Choose the command again on the landscape project and pick the next shape.
142	
143	## Undo Make Vertical
144	
145	The whole change is one undo step. In the copy, **Edit ▸ Undo Make Vertical** gives back the landscape edit. In place, it takes the command back on this project.
146	
147	## Keep the picture sharp
148	
149	A vertical canvas shows part of a landscape picture enlarged. A 1080p source framed on 1080 × 1920 is enlarged ×1.78, which can look soft on a phone, and a **Zoom** above 100 % enlarges it further. Shoot 4K for footage you mean to make vertical.
150	
151	## Good to know
152	
153	- Make Vertical works on the top-level timeline. A [nest](/editing/nests/) is treated as one clip, and what's inside it isn't reframed.
154	- If the project changes while the sheet is open or the analysis runs, nothing is made. Frame Job beeps and the foot of the inspector says "the project changed while the Make Vertical Version sheet was open, so nothing was made. Choose Make Vertical Version again." or "the project changed while Make Vertical was analyzing, so nothing was made. Choose Make Vertical Version again."
155	- If the step wouldn't change the copy, the copy is closed and nothing is made: "Make Vertical did not apply to the copy, so nothing was made."
156	
157	## With an agent
158	
159	`make_vertical_version` makes the same version from a named shape. It differs from the sheet in a few ways:
160	
161	- It can save the copy straight to a place you choose, and the assistant asks first when it does.
162	- It can leave caption tracks as placed, where the sheet always pages them again.
163	- It waits up to 60 s for an analysis. Past that nothing is made, and calling it again carries on.
164	- It takes **Zoom** as 1 to 4 rather than a percentage.
165	
166	See [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
167
