2	title: "Follow Subject"
3	description: "Frame the selected movie clips on the person or thing in them, with eased moves you can edit and a blurred copy behind where the whole picture shows."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Follow Subject keeps the person in shot when a clip's picture doesn't fit the canvas, such as a landscape recording on a 1080 × 1920 vertical canvas. It finds the subject, moves the frame with it, and writes each move as an ordinary action you can change.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Clip ▸ Follow Subject…"
14	  where="Each move, on the clip's action lane"
15	  tools="reframe_clip"
16	  needs="Nothing. Faces, people and shot changes are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
17	/>
18	
19	## Frame clips on their subject
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Set the canvas you want first, in the [Document tab](/projects/canvas-size/). Follow Subject doesn't change the canvas.
24	
25	2. Select the clips to frame.
26	
27	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**. It's available when a selected clip plays a movie and no sheet is open, inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) too. There's no keyboard shortcut.
28	
29	4. Set [Follow](#follow), [Zoom](#zoom) and [Where Empty](#where-empty).
30	
31	5. Read [the summary](#the-summary) under the controls, which says what will happen.
32	
33	6. Choose **Follow** (<kbd>Return</kbd>), or **Cancel** (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) to leave everything as it was.
34	
35	</Steps>
36	
37	<Shot
38	  name="15i-follow-subject-sheet.sheet"
39	  alt="The Follow Subject sheet, with Follow set to Subject, Zoom at 125 percent and Where Empty set to Show Whole. A summary reads: Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 1 file on this Mac first, then frames 1 clip. Cancel and Follow buttons sit at the bottom right."
40	/>
41	
42	:::tip
43	To change the canvas and frame a whole timeline in one go, use [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) instead.
44	:::
45	
46	A still, a picture, a nest, text, a shape, a graphic or an adjustment clip in the selection is left alone, with no line in the summary.
47	
48	## The controls
49	
50	### Follow
51	
52	Follow chooses what the frame stays on.
53	
54	| Choice | What the frame follows |
55	| --- | --- |
56	| **Subject** | A face, or where there's none a person, or where there's neither the region the eye goes to. This is the default. |
57	| **Faces** | Faces only |
58	| **People** | People only |
59	| **Salient Region** | Salient regions only |
60	| **Center** | Nothing. The frame holds on the middle of the picture for the whole clip, with no analysis needed. |
61	
62	### Zoom
63	
64	Zoom sets how tight the frame is, in whole percents from 100 to 400. A value outside that range is brought back to it when you leave the field. At 100 % the picture is the smallest it can be and still cover the canvas.
65	
66	It starts at 100 %. If the first selected clip's picture is within 1 % of the canvas's shape, it starts at 125 % instead, because at 100 % such a picture fills the canvas exactly and the frame has no room to move.
67	
68	Zoom enlarges the picture, and so does putting a landscape picture on a tall canvas. A 1080p source on a 1080 × 1920 canvas is already enlarged ×1.78 at 100 %.
69	
70	### Where Empty
71	
72	Where Empty sets what the frame shows while there's nothing to follow.
73	
74	| Choice | What shows |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| **Show Whole** | The whole picture, with a [blurred copy](#the-blurred-backgrounds-track) filling the canvas around it. This is the default. |
77	| **Center** | The middle of the picture, at the same zoom |
78	
79	It's dimmed while Follow is **Center**.
80	
81	### What's remembered
82	
83	**Follow** and **Where Empty** are remembered for next time, and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) shares them. They're saved when you choose **Follow**, even if you then stop the analysis, and never on **Cancel**. If Make Vertical Version last used **Speaker**, which this sheet doesn't offer, Follow opens on **Subject**. **Zoom** isn't remembered.
84	
85	## The summary
86	
87	Under the controls, the sheet says what **Follow** will do. It updates as you change a control, and after you leave the Zoom field.
88	
89	| The sheet says | What it means |
90	| --- | --- |
91	| "Frames 2 clips." | How many clips will change. |
92	| "Adds a Backgrounds track for the blurred copy." | Some of the framing shows the whole picture, so a [blurred copy](#the-blurred-backgrounds-track) goes behind it. |
93	| "Adds 1 more track behind it where clips overlap." | Two selected clips overlap in time, so their copies need separate tracks. |
94	| "2 actions re-eased at a cut." | A shot change landed inside actions the clip already had, and each was split there and eased again on either side. See [It starts from the whole picture](#it-starts-from-the-whole-picture). |
95	| "1 action carries a framing move." | A move couldn't fit between the clip's own actions, so one of them carries it. |
96	| "Clip 3 is already framed this way." | That clip wouldn't change. |
97	| "Clip 3: …" | That clip can't be framed, and this is why. See [Clips it cannot frame](#clips-it-cannot-frame). |
98	| "Reading the analysis…" | Frame Job is loading what it found earlier. **Follow** is dimmed until it's done. |
99	| "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 1 file on this Mac first, then frames 1 clip." | The [analysis comes first](#analysis-first). |
100	
101	**Follow** is dimmed when nothing would change.
102	
103	"Clip 3" uses Frame Job's own number for the clip, which isn't its position on the timeline.
104	
105	## Analysis first
106	
107	When the clips haven't been analysed, choosing **Follow** closes the sheet and opens the [Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) while Frame Job finds what it needs on your Mac. It then frames the clips by itself.
108	
109	The Analyzing sheet has a row for each file and each kind of analysis still to be made: **Shot changes**, **Faces**, and **People and salient regions**. Only the part of each file the clip plays is read, plus a second either side.
110	
111	**Stop** changes nothing. **Center** needs no analysis, so it frames at once.
112	
113	Frame Job beeps and frames nothing in these cases, and says why at the foot of the inspector, after **Refused:**
114	
115	| The inspector says | What happened |
116	| --- | --- |
117	| "the project changed while Follow Subject was analyzing, so nothing was framed. Choose Follow Subject again." | The project changed, or you went into or out of a nest, while the analysis ran. What was found is kept, so a second try doesn't start over. |
118	| "The faces analysis of “interview.mov” failed: …" | An analysis couldn't finish. The sentence names the kind and the file. |
119	
120	## It starts from the whole picture
121	
122	Each clip is framed from the whole picture. Its own positions and scales are replaced, both the clip's base values and any an action sets. An action left with nothing to do is removed. The clip's volume and its other actions stay, and so does its crop, which the frame stays inside.
123	
124	The moves then fit around the actions that remain:
125	
126	- A move goes in a gap between them.
127	- A move that would overlap an action starts up to 0.5 s earlier to clear it.
128	- A move that still can't clear is carried by the action it overlaps, along that action's curve.
129	- A shot change that lands inside an action splits it into three: the part before, the one frame of the cut, and the part after. A steady (linear) action plays as it did, and an eased one is eased again on each side.
130	- A speed action, or an action a trim left running past the clip's end, is never cut. It carries the change instead.
131	
132	## How following moves
133	
134	While it follows, the frame stays inside the picture, so nothing past the picture's edge shows.
135	
136	### Which subject it follows
137	
138	When several faces or people are in view, Frame Job scores each on how steadily it's there, how big it is and how central it is, over the second either side and within the shot.
139	
140	It stays with its choice. Another subject takes over only after scoring at least 25 % better for 2 s, so two similar faces don't trade the frame back and forth. With **Subject**, a person's body stands in for their face while the face can't be found.
141	
142	Frame Job samples the picture ten times a second, and only the first eight of each kind in a sample count. For faces, that's the eight furthest left.
143	
144	### Where the subject sits
145	
146	| Subject | Where it sits |
147	| --- | --- |
148	| A face | In the middle of the frame, or 38 % of the way down on a frame taller than wide, leaving room below for the rest of the person |
149	| A person | With the top of their box 12 % of the way down the frame |
150	| A salient region | In the middle of the frame |
151	
152	This is where the frame aims. Near the picture's edge it stops at the edge, so the subject sits off from these marks.
153	
154	### Easing and staying put
155	
156	The frame eases onto the subject and moves only when the subject leaves the middle of the frame, so a speaker who sways stays put. The middle counts as 15 % of the frame's width and 12 % of its height either side.
157	
158	A move travels at 0.8 frame widths a second and takes at least 0.4 s. No move starts within 0.5 s of the last one's end, unless the subject has left the frame altogether.
159	
160	### At a shot change
161	
162	The frame cuts with the picture, landing on the first frame of the new shot. It's placed on where the subject sits over the new shot's first second. No move runs across a cut.
163	
164	### When the subject is lost
165	
166	The frame holds for a second, so a blink or a turned head changes nothing. It then follows someone else in the shot if there's anyone. If not, it eases over 0.8 s to your [Where Empty](#where-empty) choice.
167	
168	It comes back once a subject has been in view for 0.6 s.
169	
170	A clip with nobody in view during its first second opens on Where Empty. A clip with nothing to follow at all stays on Where Empty for its whole length.
171	
172	### Two people
173	
174	The frame holds two faces or two people together when both fit in it. Each box is widened by 15 % before they're tested against the frame. Salient regions aren't paired.
175	
176	## The blurred Backgrounds track
177	
178	Where the frame shows the whole picture, the canvas shows around it. So a blurred copy of the clip goes on a new track named **Backgrounds** at the back, for the clip's whole length. That's the same copy [**Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/#blurred-background) makes: picture only, filling the canvas.
179	
180	No track is added when no clip needs one. That's always so when Follow or Where Empty is **Center**. Where two selected clips overlap in time, the second copy goes on a further new track behind Backgrounds.
181	
182	A clip with speed actions keeps them on its copy, so the copy shows the same frames.
183	
184	## Every move is an action
185	
186	Every move is an ordinary action on the clip's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/). To nudge where a frame ends, select the action and [drag the picture on the canvas](/motion/edit-an-action/#edit-on-the-canvas). You can [move, resize or remove it](/motion/change-an-action/) as you would any other.
187	
188	## Undo
189	
190	**Edit ▸ Undo Follow Subject** takes the whole command back in one step, every clip and track included. What was found stays in the cache.
191	
192	## Screen recordings are skipped
193	
194	A screen recording Frame Job made, with its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), isn't followed by faces. Follow Subject leaves it unanalysed and lists it under the summary:
195	
196	> Clip 3: clip 3's media has a cursor file, so it follows the cursor, not faces; frame it with cursor, center, fit or keep
197	
198	Of those, the sheet offers **Center**. [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) follows the pointer instead, and an agent can [follow it too](/framing/reframe-clip/).
199	
200	## Clips it cannot frame
201	
202	A selected movie clip that can't be followed gets a line under the summary, and the others are still framed. With no clip left to frame, the summary shows only those lines and **Follow** stays dimmed.
203	
204	| Clip | The line says | What you can do |
205	| --- | --- | --- |
206	| On a matte track | "clip 3 is on a matte track, which framing would move; only keep reframes it" | Change the track's [matte setting](/canvas/matte-tracks/) or move the clip |
207	| Cut by a matte | "clip 3 is cut by the matte on track 7, which framing would move it out of; only keep reframes it" | The same |
208	| Rotated | "clip 3 is turned 15°, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | Set its [rotation](/canvas/transform/) back to 0° |
209	| Turned by an action | "clip 3's action 12 turns it, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | Take rotation out of [that action](/motion/edit-an-action/#take-a-property-out-of-the-action) |
210	| Spinning | "clip 3 spins in its motion, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | [Clear the spin preset](/motion/motion-presets/#change-or-clear-a-preset) |
211	| Cropped or scaled to nothing | "clip 3's crop or scale leaves no picture to frame" | Fix its [crop](/canvas/crop/) or scale |
212	| With a cursor file | See [above](#screen-recordings-are-skipped) | Choose **Center** |
213	| With no analysis under it | "clip 3 has no subjects to follow; analyze it first" | Lengthen the clip. Frame Job samples a file ten times a second, so a very short clip can fall between two samples. |
214	
215	"keep" and the other lowercase words in these lines are an agent's options. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/).
216	
217	A clip with nobody in it isn't one of these. It's framed on your [Where Empty](#where-empty) choice.
218	
219	When an analysis has to run first, the sheet can't list these lines yet. Afterwards the clips that can be framed are framed, and the rest stay as they were with no message. If none can be, Frame Job beeps and shows the lines at the foot of the inspector.
220	
221	## Good to know
222	
223	- If a selected clip's file is missing or can't be read, the summary says so and **Follow** stays dimmed for all of them. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/), or choose **Center**, which doesn't read the file.
224	- Follow Subject doesn't frame stills or pictures. [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) can centre them.
225	- Running Follow Subject again on a clip whose frame shows the whole picture adds another Backgrounds track and another copy, and the first copy stays. Undo the first run, or delete the old copy.
226	- Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the nest's canvas is the canvas, and the Backgrounds track goes in the nest.
227	- A clip's speed, speed ramps and reversal are all taken into account, so the frame moves with what the clip shows.
228	
229	## With an agent
230	
231	`reframe_clip` frames one clip at a time. Follow Subject is that tool run on each selected clip, starting from the whole picture, with a Backgrounds track behind. The sheet's **Where Empty** is the tool's `where_empty`: `fit` for **Show Whole**, which is the default, or `center`.
232	
233	An agent has more choices than the sheet. It can show the whole picture, rescale a clip from the canvas it was made for, follow a recorded pointer or follow whoever's talking, and it can compose the framing into a clip's own moves instead of replacing them. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).

2	title: The Layout section
3	description: Pick a camera layout in the inspector, set how long the switch takes, and see what happens when a layout meets a zoom.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	The Layout section is the inspector's way to make a [camera layout](/framing/camera-layouts/) switch. It lays out the selected clip as the camera and, unlike the menu, lets you choose how long the switch takes.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸"
14	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Layout"
15	  tools="switch_layout"
16	  needs="Nothing for a layout. A crop centres on the person only when Remove Background has already made the camera's masks, on your Mac."
17	/>
18	
19	<Shot
20	  name="05j-clip-layout.inspector"
21	  alt="The Picture sub-tab scrolled to the open Layout section, its summary reading Square, Bottom Right. Layout is set to Corner, Shape to Square, Corner to Bottom Right and Duration to 0.50 s, with the Switch at Playhead button underneath."
22	/>
23	
24	## Switch at Playhead
25	
26	<Steps>
27	
28	1. Select the camera clip, and only that clip. It needs to be a clip of a video file with a picture. An image, a still or a nest gets no Layout section, though [the menu](/framing/camera-layouts/#which-clips) can lay one out.
29	
30	2. Open **Layout** in the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab. It comes after Transform and Behind Subject, and it's shut until you open it.
31	
32	3. Set the [controls](#the-controls).
33	
34	4. Move the playhead onto the clip, to where the switch should start.
35	
36	5. Press **Switch at Playhead**.
37	
38	</Steps>
39	
40	This does exactly what **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸** does, with this clip as the camera and the clip drawing behind it as the screen. It's one undo step, **Camera Layout**. Everything in [The switch](/framing/camera-layouts/#the-switch) and [How far a layout reaches](/framing/camera-layouts/#how-far-a-layout-reaches) applies.
41	
42	The button is off while a sheet is open. Pressed with the playhead off the clip, the foot of the inspector says the clip doesn't play there and nothing changes.
43	
44	## The controls
45	
46	| Control | What it does | Default | Choices |
47	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
48	| **Layout** | The layout to switch to. | Corner | Corner, Side by Side, Stacked, Camera Full, Screen Only |
49	| **Shape** | The corner picture's shape. Square is the menu's **Corner ▸**, Rounded its **Rounded Corner ▸**. Greyed for any layout but Corner. | Square | Square, Rounded, Circle |
50	| **Corner** | Which canvas corner the camera sits in. Greyed for any layout but Corner. | Bottom Right | Bottom Right, Bottom Left, Top Right, Top Left |
51	| **Duration** | How long the switch takes. | 0.5 s | 0.01 to 10 s |
52	
53	The section's header sums up what it would switch to: "Square, Bottom Right", or "Side by Side".
54	
55	Type a **Duration**, or pick 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 from the arrow in the field. A typed number outside the range goes to the nearest end of it. The switch is then rounded to whole frames, and a length under half a frame rounds to nothing, so Frame Job shows an error and doesn't switch. That's 0.01 s on a 30 fps project. At a clip's first frame the switch cuts, whatever the Duration.
56	
57	These choices belong to the section, not to the project. They stay while the window is open, they aren't saved and they aren't undo steps, so nothing changes until you press **Switch at Playhead**. There's no Reset.
58	
59	## The crop centred on the person
60	
61	Circle, Side by Side and Stacked crop the camera. When the camera's person masks already exist for every frame the clip plays, the crop centres on the person, at the middle of where the masks find them, averaged over the clip. This works from the menu and the section alike.
62	
63	[Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) makes the masks, on your Mac, and they stay in the project's cache. You can turn Remove Background off again afterwards. A layout never starts that analysis itself. With no masks, or masks for only part of the clip, the crop centres on the picture. A camera that's an image clip centres on the picture, masks or not.
64	
65	Frame Job reads the masks for a moment before it switches. If the project changes in that moment, it beeps and makes no switch. Choose the layout again.
66	
67	## A layout meets a zoom
68	
69	A switch never fights a zoom. Frame Job won't switch when a clip it would move holds a zoom or another moving action after the playhead, because the two would pull the clip in different directions.
70	
71	A moving action is any action that changes position, scale, crop, corner radius or opacity, other than a layout action. On the clip under the playhead, only an action that ends after the playhead counts, so moving the playhead past the end of a zoom clears the way. On a later clip in the layout's [reach](/framing/camera-layouts/#how-far-a-layout-reaches), any moving action counts.
72	
73	There's one exception. In Corner, Camera Full and Screen Only, a screen still at its [full placement](/framing/camera-layouts/#the-layouts) stays where it is, so its zooms keep playing and the switch goes ahead. Side by Side and Stacked always move the screen.
74	
75	When a nest would let the switch go ahead, Frame Job offers one. Otherwise the foot of the inspector names the clip and the action, and nothing changes. To make the switch anyway, move the playhead past the end of that action if it's on the clip under the playhead, or [remove the action](/motion/change-an-action/#remove-an-action), then switch again.
76	
77	## Lay out the clips in a nest?
78	
79	This sheet shows the reason the switch couldn't be made, then offers to put those clips in a [nest](/editing/nests/) first. The layout then moves the nest, and the zoom keeps playing inside it.
80	
81	- **Nest and Switch** makes the nest and the layout. One undo step, **Camera Layout**, takes both back.
82	- **Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> changes nothing.
83	
84	What goes in the nest is the clip at the playhead and the later clips in the layout's reach, apart from a clip that holds the next switch. Only the side that stopped the switch is nested, so a screen that zooms is nested and its camera isn't. If both the camera and the screen hold a moving action, each gets a nest of its own.
85	
86	There's no offer when:
87	
88	- one of those clips is already laid out, because a nest would lay it out twice. That includes a clip that sits anywhere but its [full placement](/framing/camera-layouts/#the-layouts), such as a camera a recording landed in the corner
89	- the camera holds the moving action and you chose Rounded Corner or Circle, because a nest clip shows square corners only
90	
91	When the camera itself goes into a nest, its crop centres on the nest's picture rather than the person.
92	
93	## With an agent
94	
95	An agent is never shown the sheet. It asks for the nest in the same `switch_layout` call, and Frame Job won't do that when one of the clips is already laid out.
96	
97	An agent can also centre the camera's crop on a point of its own choosing, and that point stays as sent even when the camera goes into a nest. If it doesn't choose one, the crop is filled from the masks as it is for the menu, and the call's answer gives the centre it used. See [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
98

2	title: Make Vertical Version
3	description: Turn a landscape edit into a tall or square version for a phone, a reel or a square post, in one step over the whole timeline.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Make Vertical Version makes a tall or square version of a landscape edit, for a phone, a reel or a square post. It changes the canvas and reworks the whole timeline in one step, so you don't have to frame each clip yourself.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
14	  tools="make_vertical_version"
15	  needs="Nothing. Faces, people and shot changes are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
16	/>
17	
18	## Make a vertical version
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Choose **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**. It has no keyboard shortcut. It's available when the project has a clip, no [nest](/editing/nests/) is open, no other sheet is up and nothing is recording.
23	
24	2. Pick a [**Shape**](#shape).
25	
26	3. Choose what to [**Follow**](#follow), and set [**Zoom**](#zoom) and [**Where Empty**](#where-empty) if you want to.
27	
28	4. Leave [**Make a copy**](#make-a-copy) ticked to keep this project as it is, or untick it to change this project.
29	
30	5. [Read the summary](#read-the-summary) under the controls. It says what will happen before anything does.
31	
32	6. Choose **Make** (<kbd>Return</kbd>), or **Cancel** (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) to leave everything as it was.
33	
34	</Steps>
35	
36	<Shot
37	  name="15j-make-vertical-sheet.sheet"
38	  alt="The Make Vertical Version sheet, with Shape on 9:16 (540 × 960), Follow on Subject, Zoom at 100 %, Where Empty on Show Whole and Make a copy ticked. The summary under them reads: Makes a 540 × 960 version. Keeps 4 clips as placed."
39	/>
40	
41	Each clip is treated by what it is: full-frame movies follow their subject, screen recordings follow the pointer, camera layouts are laid out again, and so on. [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/) goes through it clip by clip.
42	
43	## The controls
44	
45	### Shape
46	
47	Each row shows the size it makes, such as **9:16 (1080 × 1920)**. The new canvas keeps the old short side, rounded down to an even number, and the height follows from the shape.
48	
49	| Shape | From 1920 × 1080 |
50	| --- | --- |
51	| **9:16** | 1080 × 1920 |
52	| **4:5** | 1080 × 1350 |
53	| **1:1** | 1080 × 1080 |
54	
55	A shape the canvas already has isn't in the list.
56	
57	### Follow
58	
59	What each movie clip keeps in the frame.
60	
61	| Choice | What the frame follows |
62	| --- | --- |
63	| **Subject** | A face. Where there's no face, a person. Where there's neither, the region the eye goes to. |
64	| **Faces** | Faces only. |
65	| **People** | People only. |
66	| **Salient Region** | Only the region the eye goes to. |
67	| **Speaker** | Whoever is talking, for a wide shot with a microphone per person. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/). |
68	| **Center** | The middle of the picture, for the whole clip. Needs no analysis, so the summary is ready at once. |
69	
70	These are the choices of [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/), plus **Speaker**. The two commands share one remembered choice, saved when you choose **Make**. It starts on **Subject**. If you last chose **Speaker**, Follow Subject, which doesn't offer it, opens on **Subject**.
71	
72	### Zoom
73	
74	How tight the frame is, from 100 to 400 %, in whole numbers. 100 % is the smallest scale at which a picture covers the new canvas. Higher values frame closer.
75	
76	**Zoom** starts at 100 % each time you choose the command and isn't remembered. The one exception is the sheet that [comes back after a Speaker analysis](/framing/follow-speaker/#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis), which keeps what you set. The summary updates when you leave the field.
77	
78	### Where Empty
79	
80	What a followed clip shows while there's nothing to follow.
81	
82	| Choice | What the frame shows |
83	| --- | --- |
84	| **Show Whole** | The whole picture on a blurred copy of itself. This is the default. |
85	| **Center** | The middle of the picture. |
86	
87	It's dimmed while **Follow** is **Center**. It's the same remembered choice as Follow Subject's.
88	
89	### Make a copy
90	
91	Ticked, the vertical version opens as a new untitled project and this project doesn't change. The copy is named after this project with the shape, such as "Interview (9:16)", "Interview (4:5)" or "Interview (1:1)". It carries the project's caches and analysis. Save it when you want to keep it.
92	
93	Unticked, this project itself becomes the vertical version.
94	
95	The box is ticked each time you choose the command, and your choice isn't remembered. Only the sheet that comes back after a Speaker analysis keeps what you chose.
96	
97	## Read the summary
98	
99	Under the controls, the sheet says what **Make** will do, and it changes as you change a control. It opens with the new size, "Makes a 1080 × 1920 version.", and goes on with whichever of these apply:
100	
101	| The summary says | What it means |
102	| --- | --- |
103	| "Follows 3 clips." | Movie clips that follow what you chose. |
104	| "Follows the cursor in 2 clips, their own zooms and pans replaced." | Screen recordings that follow the pointer. |
105	| "Follows whoever is talking in 1 clip." | Wide shots framed on the speaker. |
106	| "Re-lays 2 camera layouts for the new canvas." | Camera layout switches made again. |
107	| "Shows 1 clip whole on a blurred copy." | Clips with nothing to follow at any point. |
108	| "Keeps 4 clips as placed." | Clips moved and scaled to the new canvas, not framed. |
109	| "Re-fills 1 background." | Blurred copies and background plates resized to cover the new canvas. |
110	| "Removes 1 blurred copy the framing replaces." | Old blurred copies that are no longer needed. |
111	| "Re-sizes 1 graphic to the new canvas." | Graphics exactly the old canvas's size. |
112	| "Updates 1 graphic module to the current template." | Older copies of a bundled template, in a copy only. |
113	| "Adds a Backgrounds track for the blurred copy." | A new track at the back for the blurred copies. |
114	| "Adds 1 more track behind it where clips overlap." | A further track, for copies that overlap in time. |
115	| "2 actions re-eased at a cut." | A shot change landed inside actions a clip already had, so each was split there and eased again on either side. |
116	| "2 actions carry a framing move." | A framing move couldn't fit between a clip's own actions, so those actions carry it. |
117	| "Re-lays 1 caption track for the new canvas." | Word captions paged again for the narrow frame. |
118	
119	After those come single lines for what needs your attention:
120	
121	- One line per camera layout switch: "Re-laid: Side by Side → Stacked at 00:00:10:00."
122	- One line per clip that isn't followed, or is only partly followed, with the reason: "Clip 6 is not followed: its media file is missing, so it is kept as placed." or "Clip 2 is followed, but it is shown whole on a blurred copy where no subject is found."
123	- One line per caption track that's kept as it was, and one per graphic module left as it is.
124	
125	If the movies have already been analysed, the summary reads "Reading the analysis…" for a moment, and **Make** is dimmed until it's done.
126	
127	If Frame Job can't make the new version, the summary says why and **Make** stays dimmed. When an analysis has to run first, Frame Job beeps after it instead and says why at the foot of the inspector. A project at its limit of 64 tracks, nests included, is one such case, because Make Vertical needs a track for the blurred copies.
128	
129	## When the movies need analysing
130	
131	Following a subject needs to know where the faces, people and shot changes are. When the movies haven't been analysed yet, the summary says so: "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 3 files on this Mac first, then makes a 1080 × 1920 version."
132	
133	**Make** then shows the Analyzing sheet while that runs on your Mac, and makes the version when it's done. **Stop** makes nothing: no project opens and this one doesn't change.
134	
135	**Center** needs no analysis, and a recording that follows its pointer is never analysed. With **Speaker**, the sheet comes back after the analysis so you can [confirm who is on each microphone](/framing/follow-speaker/#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis).
136	
137	If an analysis fails, Frame Job beeps, makes nothing and names the file at the foot of the inspector.
138	
139	## Make another shape
140	
141	What was found stays in this project's cache and is carried into the copy, so making another shape afterwards needs no analysis. Choose the command again on the landscape project and pick the next shape.
142	
143	## Undo Make Vertical
144	
145	The whole change is one undo step. In the copy, **Edit ▸ Undo Make Vertical** gives back the landscape edit. In place, it takes the command back on this project.
146	
147	## Keep the picture sharp
148	
149	A vertical canvas shows part of a landscape picture enlarged. A 1080p source framed on 1080 × 1920 is enlarged ×1.78, which can look soft on a phone, and a **Zoom** above 100 % enlarges it further. Shoot 4K for footage you mean to make vertical.
150	
151	## Good to know
152	
153	- Make Vertical works on the top-level timeline. A [nest](/editing/nests/) is treated as one clip, and what's inside it isn't reframed.
154	- If the project changes while the sheet is open or the analysis runs, nothing is made. Frame Job beeps and the foot of the inspector says "the project changed while the Make Vertical Version sheet was open, so nothing was made. Choose Make Vertical Version again." or "the project changed while Make Vertical was analyzing, so nothing was made. Choose Make Vertical Version again."
155	- If the step wouldn't change the copy, the copy is closed and nothing is made: "Make Vertical did not apply to the copy, so nothing was made."
156	
157	## With an agent
158	
159	`make_vertical_version` makes the same version from a named shape. It differs from the sheet in a few ways:
160	
161	- It can save the copy straight to a place you choose, and the assistant asks first when it does.
162	- It can leave caption tracks as placed, where the sheet always pages them again.
163	- It waits up to 60 s for an analysis. Past that nothing is made, and calling it again carries on.
164	- It takes **Zoom** as 1 to 4 rather than a percentage.
165	
166	See [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
167

1	---
2	title: "Reframe a clip (agents)"
3	description: How an agent frames one clip on the canvas, from following a face, a pointer or whoever is talking to rescaling it from an older canvas.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	`reframe_clip` is how an agent fits one clip to the current canvas, say a landscape recording on a 1080 × 1920 canvas. The agent can be the [Assistant](/assistant/chat/) or [one you connect yourself](/mcp/overview/). [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) frame clips the same way, and this page is for when you want an agent to do it one clip at a time, with every choice in its hands.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…']}
13	  tools={['reframe_clip', 'set_canvas', 'undo']}
14	  needs="Nothing to set up. Faces, people and salient regions are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
15	/>
16	
17	## Frame a clip
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Set the [canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/) you want, because the frame is worked out for the current canvas. An agent does this with `set_canvas`, leaving `rescale_clips` off. Inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/), the nest's canvas is the canvas.
22	
23	2. Ask the agent to frame the clip and say what to follow, for example "follow the face in this clip". It calls `reframe_clip` with the `clip` and what to `follow`, and everything else is optional:
24	
25	   ```json
26	   { "clip": 12, "follow": "face", "zoom": 1.5 }
27	   ```
28	
29	3. If the agent says the clip is [still being analysed](#waiting-for-analysis), have it call again.
30	
31	4. Play the clip back. **Edit ▸ Undo Reframe Clip** takes the whole framing back.
32	
33	</Steps>
34	
35	A framing that would leave the clip exactly as it is changes nothing, and the agent is told the project is already in that state. There's no undo step for it. [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/#reframe_clip) lists every argument.
36	
37	## Choose what to follow
38	
39	| `follow` | What the frame does | Analysis |
40	| --- | --- | --- |
41	| `subject` | Follows a face, else a person, else a salient region | Yes |
42	| `face`, `person`, `salient` | Follows only that kind | Yes |
43	| `cursor` | Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer | None, reads the cursor file |
44	| `speaker` | Cuts to whoever is talking in a wide shot | Yes, and the microphones' speech |
45	| `center` | Holds on the middle of the picture | None |
46	| `fit` | Shows the whole picture | None |
47	| `layout` | Lays camera layouts out again on this canvas | None |
48	| `keep` | Rescales the clip from an older canvas | None |
49	
50	The first four rows move the frame over time. The sheets don't offer all of these. **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** has Subject, Faces, People, Salient Region and Center, **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** adds Speaker, and Make Vertical uses `cursor`, `fit`, `layout` and `keep` by itself where a clip calls for them. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).
51	
52	### `subject`
53	
54	Follows a face. Where there's no face it follows a person, and where there's neither it follows a salient region, the part of the picture that draws the eye. This is **Subject** in [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/), and [How a followed frame moves](#how-a-followed-frame-moves) says what the frame does.
55	
56	### `face`, `person` and `salient`
57	
58	Each follows only that kind. Where there's none to follow, the frame behaves as it does [when a subject is lost](#how-a-followed-frame-moves). These are **Faces**, **People** and **Salient Region** on the Follow Subject sheet.
59	
60	A clip whose media has a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) can't use `subject` or these three, because a recording with a cursor file follows its cursor, never faces.
61	
62	### `cursor`
63	
64	Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer, from its media's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). A screen recording made by Frame Job has one.
65	
66	- The frame sits on the pointer and moves only when the pointer strays more than 20 % of the frame's width, or 12 % of its height, from the middle.
67	- A click outside that area gets there in time: the move ends on the click's frame.
68	- The frame holds still while you type. A click during typing still moves it.
69	
70	It needs no analysis, so it never waits. The frame never shows the whole picture, so `where_empty` and `backdrop` do nothing here.
71	
72	If the cursor file is missing or won't open, the agent is told which file and why. The **Cursor** section of the Media tab has **Locate…** to point the media at a moved file.
73	
74	### `speaker`
75	
76	Frames a wide shot of two to four people on whoever is talking. Each person needs a microphone of their own, and the agent names those clips in `mics`: a clip of a sound file or a camera's detached sound for each, each on its own track.
77	
78	- **Who talks when** is read from the microphones exactly as [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) reads them with its default settings, so the two agree.
79	- **Whose face is whose** comes from matching each microphone to the face whose mouth moves while it talks. Faces are numbered 1, 2 and so on from left to right, and a face has to be in view for at least a quarter of the clip to count.
80	- **Each change of speaker** is a cut, held at least 2 s.
81	- **Two people talking at once** are framed together when they fit. Otherwise the frame stays on whichever of them is already framed, or goes to the first of them in `mics`.
82	- **While nobody talks**, the last speaker stays.
83	
84	**File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** has this as Follow **Speaker**, with the microphones and faces confirmed on the sheet. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/).
85	
86	When the mouths don't move closely enough with the microphones, Frame Job can't tell who is whose. The agent is told where each face is across the picture, for example "face 1 at 28 % across the picture, face 2 at 71 %". It then names each microphone's face in `mic_faces`, in the same order as `mics`, and calls again.
87	
88	Frame Job won't frame on the speaker when:
89	
90	| The problem | What to do |
91	| --- | --- |
92	| `mics` doesn't hold two to four clips, or names a clip twice | Name each microphone once |
93	| A microphone is the clip being framed, or has no sound from a media file | Use a clip of a sound file, or a camera's detached sound |
94	| A microphone's sound is off | Turn it on, or leave it out of `mics` |
95	| Two microphones are on one track | Give each its own track |
96	| `mic_faces` has the wrong count, a face 0, a face twice, or a number past the faces shown | Name one different face for each microphone |
97	| A microphone is still being measured | Try again in a moment. Frame Job measures loudness and speech when a file is added |
98	| A microphone has no speech over the clip | Leave it out, or check it's the right clip |
99	| The clip changes shot | Split it first with [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/) |
100	| Fewer faces show than there are microphones | Use fewer microphones, or a shot that shows everyone |
101	| Nobody speaks inside the clip | Frame the clip another way |
102	
103	`speaker` works on what's open in the window, so a call addressed to a nest that isn't open stops and says to open it with `set_scope` first.
104	
105	### `center`
106	
107	Holds the frame on the middle of the picture for the whole clip. It needs no analysis, and it uses `zoom`.
108	
109	### `fit`
110	
111	Shows the whole picture for the whole clip, scaled to fit the canvas. It needs no analysis and ignores `zoom`. It has no menu choice of its own, but Make Vertical uses it for a recording whose cursor file can't be read.
112	
113	### `layout`
114	
115	Lays a camera clip's [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/), and its screen's, out again on the current canvas, as Make Vertical Version does. The agent can name the camera or the screen, and both change.
116	
117	Frame Job looks at each layout switch made on the old canvas, `from_width` × `from_height`, and works out which layout it was. Its position, crop and corner radius have to match that layout to within 1 px, and its scale and opacity to within 0.001. The switch is then made again on this canvas, at the same time and with the same length and curve. Without those two arguments the old canvas is taken to be the current one.
118	
119	- **Side by Side** becomes **Stacked** on a canvas taller than wide.
120	- The cut pieces of the recording take the new layout.
121	- Any zoom on them is adjusted so it shows the same part of the picture.
122	
123	It ignores `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` and `replace`.
124	
125	Frame Job won't do this for a clip with no camera layout, a clip laid out both as a camera and as a screen, a screen layout with no camera switch in front of it, or a switch edited by hand. The agent is told the clip, and the action when one switch is the problem. For a clip with no layout it can use `subject`, `center`, `fit` or `keep`, and the clip stays as placed until it does.
126	
127	### `keep`
128	
129	Rescales the clip from the canvas it was placed on, `from_width` × `from_height`, to the current one, as `set_canvas` does with `rescale_clips`. Its position follows each axis's change and its scale follows the smaller of the two, and every position and scale its actions set moves with it. Each argument defaults to the current canvas's size, so with neither there's nothing to rescale.
130	
131	It needs no analysis and ignores `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` and `replace`.
132	
133	It works on every clip the other kinds turn down, as long as the clip has a picture. Make Vertical keeps titles, shapes and other clips this way.
134	
135	## How a followed frame moves
136	
137	With `subject`, `face`, `person` and `salient`, the frame:
138	
139	- eases onto the subject and moves only when the subject leaves the middle of the frame, so a speaker who sways stays put
140	- cuts with the picture at each shot change, landing on the first frame of the new shot
141	- holds for 1 s when the subject is lost, so a blink or a turned head changes nothing
142	- then follows someone else in the shot, or eases over 0.8 s to what `where_empty` says
143	- comes back once a subject has been in view for 0.6 s
144	- frames two people together when both fit in the frame
145	
146	[How following moves](/framing/follow-subject/#how-following-moves) has the detail.
147	
148	`where_empty` is what the frame shows where there's nothing to follow: `fit`, the whole picture and the default, or `center`, the middle of the picture. These are **Show Whole** and **Center** on the Follow Subject sheet. A clip with nothing to follow anywhere in it shows this for its whole length.
149	
150	## Set how tight the frame is
151	
152	`zoom` is how tight the frame is, from 1 to 4. At 1, the default, the picture is at the scale that fills the canvas. At 2 it's twice that scale.
153	
154	`center`, `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor` and `speaker` use it. A value outside 1 to 4 stops the call whichever kind it asks for.
155	
156	## Put a blurred copy behind the clip
157	
158	Where the framing shows the whole picture, the canvas shows around it. Name a track behind the clip as `backdrop` and a blurred copy of the clip goes there for the clip's whole length. It's the copy **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** makes. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
159	
160	- With no `backdrop`, there's no copy.
161	- A copy is made only when the framing shows the whole picture somewhere: with `fit`, or with a followed clip that falls back to the whole picture.
162	- If the named track is locked, a matte, or busy over the clip, the copy goes on a new track at the back instead.
163	- A clip with speed actions keeps them on its copy, so the copy shows the same frames.
164	- The result gives the copy's id in `new_clips`, and the track's in `new_tracks` when it needed a new one.
165	
166	## Written as ordinary edits
167	
168	The framing is written as the clip's position and scale, and one action per move, each of which you can change afterwards like any other [action](/motion/actions/). You'll see them on the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/).
169	
170	**Edit ▸ Undo Reframe Clip** takes the whole framing back in one step, and so does the agent's `undo`.
171	
172	## A clip that already has actions
173	
174	A clip keeps the actions it has. The framing is composed into them, so a zoom or pan the clip already makes still happens, inside the new framing, and a volume or speed action still does what it did.
175	
176	The framing's own moves go in the gaps between the clip's actions. A move that would overlap one is moved up to half a second earlier, or else made part of that action, along its curve.
177	
178	A shot change that falls inside an action cuts the action in three around the one-frame cut. A steady change of volume still sounds exactly as it did, and an eased one eases again on each side of the cut. A speed action, or one a trim left running past the clip's end, is never cut, and takes the framing's change across its length instead.
179	
180	### Start from the whole picture
181	
182	With `replace` set to true, the framing replaces the clip's own moves instead of working inside them. Every position and scale the clip's actions set is removed, the picture is fitted to the canvas, and then the clip is framed. Volume and everything else stay, and an action left with nothing is removed.
183	
184	The default is false. Every kind uses it but `keep` and `layout`. **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** always starts from the whole picture this way, with a **Backgrounds** track as its `backdrop`, as one undo step named **Follow Subject**.
185	
186	## Which options each kind reads
187	
188	| `follow` | `zoom` | `where_empty` | `backdrop` | `replace` | `from_width`, `from_height` |
189	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
190	| `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
191	| `speaker` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
192	| `cursor` | Yes | No | No | Yes | No |
193	| `center` | Yes | No | No | Yes | No |
194	| `fit` | No | No | Yes | Yes | No |
195	| `layout` | No | No | No | No | Yes |
196	| `keep` | No | No | No | No | Yes |
197	
198	`mics` and `mic_faces` belong to `speaker` alone. An option a kind doesn't use is ignored, except that a `zoom` outside 1 to 4, a `from_width` or `from_height` of 0 and an unknown `backdrop` track stop the call whatever the kind.
199	
200	## Waiting for analysis
201	
202	If the part of the file the clip plays hasn't been analysed, the tool analyses it and waits up to a minute. It looks at that part with a second either side, for shots, faces and subjects, on your Mac. In the result, `cached` is false when an analysis ran first. A clip that can't be framed for another reason is turned down straight away, without waiting.
203	
204	If a minute isn't enough, nothing changes and the analysis carries on. The result still says `ok: true`, with an `analyzing` entry naming the files still going and how much is covered, so an agent has to look for it. It then calls again to apply the framing. [The analysis wait](/mcp/tools-framing/#the-analysis-wait) has the details.
205	
206	- `center`, `fit`, `keep`, `cursor` and `layout` need no analysis, so they never wait.
207	- `speaker` also needs its microphones' loudness and speech, which Frame Job measures when a file is added.
208	- If the project or the open nest changes while the tool reads the analysis, nothing is framed and the agent is told to call again.
209	- If the analysis fails, nothing is framed and the agent is told which analysis and why.
210	- [Stopping the Assistant](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) during the wait frames nothing.
211	
212	## When a clip can't be framed
213	
214	A clip that can't be framed is left as it was, and the agent gets a sentence saying why. Frame Job checks in this order and stops at the first one that applies.
215	
216	| The clip | Which kinds it stops | What still works |
217	| --- | --- | --- |
218	| A text, shape, graphic or adjustment clip | All but `keep` | `keep` |
219	| Has no picture, or a crop or scale leaves none | All | Nothing |
220	| A nest clip, then a still or image clip | `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor`, `speaker` | `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
221	| Its media has no cursor file | `cursor` | `subject`, `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
222	| Its media has a cursor file | `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `speaker` | `cursor`, `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
223	| On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), or cut by a matte | All but `keep` and `layout` | `keep` |
224	| Turned: a rotation, an action turning it, or a spin in its motion | All but `keep` and `layout` | `keep` |
225	| With a copy to make, a nest clip, or a `backdrop` track that isn't behind the clip's | Any kind that makes a copy | Leave `backdrop` out, or name a track further back |
226	| Analysis holds nothing for the part of the clip that plays, or no recorded pointer falls inside it | `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor` | `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
227	
228	`layout` has [its own checks](#layout), and it skips the matte and turned rows. [`speaker`'s checks](#speaker) come after the turned clip.
229	
230	Before any of that, a call stops on a value it can't use: an unknown clip, track or microphone, or a `from_width` or `from_height` of 0.

2	title: "Show Subjects"
3	description: "Draw the faces, people and salient regions Frame Job has found for a clip over the preview, so you can see what framing will follow."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Show Subjects outlines what Frame Job has found in the selected clip at the playhead, right on the preview. Use it to check what [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) has to work with.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="View ▸ Show Subjects"
13	  needs="Nothing. It only draws what has already been found."
14	/>
15	
16	## Turn on Show Subjects
17	
18	<Steps>
19	
20	1. Select a clip of a movie.
21	
22	2. Move the playhead to a moment that clip shows.
23	
24	3. Choose **View ▸ Show Subjects**. A tick appears beside it in the menu.
25	
26	</Steps>
27	
28	If a note appears instead of boxes, the clip hasn't been analysed yet. See [Not analyzed](#not-analyzed).
29	
30	Select another clip to see its boxes, and move the playhead to see another moment. Choose the item again to turn it off.
31	
32	The item has no shortcut, and it's available whenever the window has no sheet open.
33	
34	It draws for one clip at a time. With several clips selected, that's the front-most one showing at the playhead. A selected still, picture, nest, text, shape or graphic draws nothing and shows no note, and neither does a clip the playhead isn't on.
35	
36	## What the outlines mean
37	
38	| Outline | What it marks |
39	| --- | --- |
40	| Yellow | A face |
41	| Teal | A person's head and shoulders |
42	| Purple, dashed | A salient region, a part of the picture the eye goes to first |
43	
44	Each outline has a dark line behind it, so it stays visible on a bright picture. Faces draw on top of the other two.
45	
46	[Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/) explains what each kind of box is.
47	
48	## The boxes stay on the picture
49	
50	The boxes sit on the clip's picture wherever you've placed it. If you've moved, scaled or rotated the clip, each box moves and turns with it. If you've cropped the clip, the boxes are clipped to the crop.
51	
52	They also follow the clip's speed, speed ramps and reversal, so they show what the clip is showing at that moment rather than what's at the same time in the file.
53	
54	## Not analyzed
55	
56	When nothing has been found for the clip's picture at the playhead, a note sits at the clip's top-left corner:
57	
58	> Not analyzed — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… analyzes it
59	
60	Show Subjects never starts an analysis, so turning it on costs nothing. To make the boxes, run [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) or [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) on the clip. If Show Subjects is on when an analysis lands, the boxes appear by themselves.
61	
62	Three situations are worth knowing:
63	
64	- Analysis covers the parts of a file that clips play, plus a second either side. Another part of the same file can still read "Not analyzed".
65	- A part that's been analysed and holds nothing shows no outlines and no note.
66	- Follow Subject doesn't analyse a screen recording that has its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), so the note stays on such a clip. See [Screen recordings are skipped](/framing/follow-subject/#screen-recordings-are-skipped).
67	
68	## A view of the window
69	
70	Show Subjects belongs to the window, not the project. It's off in a new window, each window has its own setting, and it isn't remembered between launches. It edits nothing, so it isn't an undo step, and it never changes an export or a saved frame.
71	
72	## With an agent
73	
74	There's no agent tool for the overlay. An agent reads the same boxes with `get_media_analysis`. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
75

1	---
2	title: What Make Vertical changes
3	description: Clip by clip, what Make Vertical Version does to movies, screen recordings, camera layouts, stills, graphics, captions and everything else.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	[Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) doesn't crop the timeline as one picture. It looks at each clip and treats it by what it is, so a talking head follows its subject while a title stays a title. This page says what happens to each kind of clip, and what the sheet's summary says about it.
9	
10	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…" tools={['make_vertical_version', 'reframe_clip']} />
11	
12	## How a clip is judged
13	
14	Every clip with a picture on the top-level timeline is judged on the old canvas. The first row that fits decides what happens to it.
15	
16	| The clip | What happens |
17	| --- | --- |
18	| A [blurred copy](#blurred-copies-and-background-plates) behind a clip | Removed, or re-filled to cover the new canvas |
19	| A [background plate](#blurred-copies-and-background-plates) | Re-filled to cover the new canvas |
20	| A [graphic exactly the old canvas's size](#graphics) | Re-sized to the new canvas |
21	| A [camera or a screen in a camera layout](#camera-layouts) | Laid out again for the new canvas |
22	| A [screen recording with its cursor file](#screen-recordings) that fills the frame | Follows the pointer |
23	| A [movie](#full-frame-movies) that fills the frame | Follows its subject |
24	| A [still, picture or nest](#stills-pictures-and-nests) that fills the frame | Centred |
25	| [Word captions](#word-captions) | Paged again for the narrow frame |
26	| [Everything else](#everything-else) | Kept as placed |
27	
28	A clip **fills the old frame** when its rectangle at its first frame covers the canvas on one side, to within a pixel at each edge, and on the other side is centred to within 2 % or covers that too. So the usual full-frame shot counts, and so does one punched in a little. A picture-in-picture doesn't.
29	
30	A sound-only clip, a clip with its video turned off and an adjustment clip have no picture here, so nothing happens to them.
31	
32	## Full-frame movies
33	
34	A movie clip that fills the old frame follows what you chose in **Follow**, as [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) frames it. Its own moves and actions stay, inside the framing.
35	
36	Where the frame shows the whole picture, a blurred copy of the clip goes behind it, so the canvas around it isn't empty. The copies go on a new **Backgrounds** track at the back, and copies that overlap in time go on further tracks behind it. The track is removed when no copy needs it.
37	
38	The summary tells you how each one went:
39	
40	| The clip | The summary says |
41	| --- | --- |
42	| Follows its subject | It's counted in "Follows 3 clips." |
43	| Has nothing to follow at any point | It's counted in "Shows 1 clip whole on a blurred copy." |
44	| Has nothing to follow for part of its length | It's still counted as followed, with "Clip 2 is followed, but it is shown whole on a blurred copy where no subject is found." |
45	| Moves by a [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/) of its own | "Clip 2 is followed, but moves by its own motion: …", with the preset's name, because that move isn't part of the framing. |
46	
47	Some movies can't be followed and are kept as placed, each listed with the reason:
48	
49	- A movie whose file is missing: "Clip 6 is not followed: its media file is missing, so it is kept as placed." With **Follow** on **Center** it's centred like any other clip instead.
50	- A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), or one a matte cuts, because framing would move it out of the matte.
51	- A clip turned by its rotation or by an action, or one that spins in its motion, because framing works on an upright picture.
52	
53	With **Follow** on **Speaker**, a wide shot beside its microphones cuts to whoever is talking, and every other movie follows its faces. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/).
54	
55	## Screen recordings
56	
57	A screen recording with its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) follows the pointer instead of a face, because a face on a screen isn't what the viewer is looking at.
58	
59	- The frame sits on the pointer and moves only when it strays from the middle of the frame, by more than 20 % of the frame's width or 12 % of its height.
60	- It arrives on a click outside that area. The move ends on the click's frame, so the click lands in view.
61	- It holds still while you type.
62	- Any zoom and pan of the clip's own, such as [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/)'s, is replaced, since the tall frame is already a close-up. The summary says so: "Follows the cursor in 2 clips, their own zooms and pans replaced."
63	
64	**Where Empty** doesn't apply to a recording that follows its pointer. **Center** centres the recording as any other movie.
65	
66	When the cursor file can't be read, because it was moved or deleted, the recording is shown whole on a blurred copy and the summary says "its cursor file could not be read, so it is shown whole".
67	
68	## Camera layouts
69	
70	A screen recording and its camera in [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) keep their arrangement. This covers the layouts of **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸** and the layout a recording landed in. Each switch is made again for the new canvas, at the same time, length and curve.
71	
72	| On the old canvas | On the new canvas |
73	| --- | --- |
74	| A Corner | A Corner in the same corner |
75	| Camera Full | Camera Full |
76	| Side by Side, going to a tall canvas | Stacked, with the screen across the top and the camera below it, so the screen isn't squeezed into two-thirds of a narrow frame |
77	| Side by Side, going to a square | Side by Side |
78	
79	The camera, the screen and the cut pieces of either are never followed and get no blurred copy. A zoom on the screen keeps showing the same part of the picture.
80	
81	The summary counts them, "Re-lays 2 camera layouts for the new canvas.", and lists each switch: "Re-laid: Side by Side → Stacked at 00:00:10:00."
82	
83	A circle or panel crop is re-centred on the middle of the crop it had. A crop that had room to move may sit nearer the middle of the camera picture than a switch made directly on the new canvas would.
84	
85	### A layout changed by hand
86	
87	If a camera was moved or resized by more than a pixel after its switch, it's no longer a layout Frame Job made. The camera and its screen are kept as placed, and the summary says "Clip 6 is not followed: its camera layout was edited by hand, so it is kept as placed."
88	
89	## Stills, pictures and nests
90	
91	A still or a picture that fills the frame is centred, and so is a [nest](/editing/nests/) that does. There's nothing inside them to follow. The summary lists each one: "Clip 4 is not followed: it is a still picture, so it is centred." or "Clip 4 is not followed: it is a nest, so it is centred."
92	
93	What's inside a nest isn't reframed. A still, picture or nest that doesn't fill the frame is [kept as placed](#everything-else).
94	
95	## Graphics
96	
97	A graphic exactly the old canvas's size, such as a full-frame lower third or title card, is re-sized to the new canvas, so it lays itself out again on the narrow frame. Its position, and the positions its actions move it to, shrink and stretch with the two sides. Its scale stays as it was. Any other graphic is [kept as placed](#everything-else).
98	
99	Older copies of the bundled templates in the project are updated in a copy, and listed when you apply the step in place: "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it is an older copy of the bundled template "lower-third"; Make Vertical updates it only in a copy." A module of your own that sizes itself by the canvas's height is listed too, and never rewritten. See [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/).
100	
101	## Everything else
102	
103	Titles, other graphics, shapes, a picture-in-picture and any clip that doesn't fill the frame are kept as placed. They're moved and scaled from the old canvas to the new one, as the Document tab does when a [canvas change](/projects/canvas-size/) rescales clips:
104	
105	- A clip's horizontal position follows the change in width.
106	- Its vertical position follows the change in height.
107	- Its scale follows the smaller of the two changes, so something that fitted the old canvas still fits the new one.
108	
109	From 1920 × 1080 to 1080 × 1920, a title's distance from the centre shrinks to 0.56 across and grows to 1.78 down, and the title itself shrinks to 0.56 of its size. The positions and scales its actions move to change the same way.
110	
111	## Blurred copies and background plates
112	
113	A blurred copy already behind a clip is removed when that clip is framed, because the framing makes a new one where it's needed. Otherwise it's re-filled to cover the new canvas. A copy counts as one when it's named **Blurred Background** and a clip of the same source, start and length sits in front of it.
114	
115	A background plate from **Clip ▸ Add Background** is re-filled too. A plate is a rectangle shape the canvas's size, centred at scale 1, or an image or still named **Background** that fills the canvas. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
116	
117	## Word captions
118	
119	Word captions are split into pages again for the narrow frame, from the words their pages already hold, as **File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas** does. Every correction you typed is kept, but the new pages are drawn fresh from the style, so a colour or position you changed on a page goes. A track that was hidden or locked stays that way. See [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/).
120	
121	A caption track that can't be re-laid is kept as placed, and the summary names it: "Caption track "Captions 2" is kept as placed: it holds a page with no word timings." That happens to [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/), and to a track when:
122	
123	- it's a matte track
124	- a page has no word timings, or none of a page's words starts inside it
125	- a page is in a style Frame Job doesn't make, or its pages are in more than one style
126	- its pages wouldn't fit
127	
128	## With an agent
129	
130	`make_vertical_version` tells the agent how each clip was treated and why, which clips followed their pointer, and each layout switch it made again. It can also leave caption tracks as placed, where the sheet always pages them again. `reframe_clip` applies one of these framings to a single clip. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
131

1	---
2	title: "Subjects in the picture"
3	description: "What Frame Job finds in a clip's picture on this Mac, what it doesn't know about the people in it, and when a file gets analysed."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Frame Job can find who and what is in a clip's picture: faces, people and the parts the eye goes to first. Its framing tools use this to keep a subject in shot on a canvas of a different shape.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…', 'View ▸ Show Subjects']}
12	  tools={['get_media_analysis', 'reframe_clip', 'make_vertical_version']}
13	  needs="Nothing. Apple's Vision framework does this on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
14	/>
15	
16	## What is found
17	
18	Frame Job samples the picture ten times a second of the file's own time, so a clip you've slowed down or sped up doesn't change what's found. It keeps three things from each sample.
19	
20	### Faces
21	
22	Each face's box, how it's turned, and how open the mouth is. Faces in a sample are listed from left to right. An agent reads them with `get_media_analysis`, kind `faces`. See [Faces](/projects/media-analysis/#faces) under media analysis.
23	
24	### People
25	
26	Each person's head and shoulders, as a box. A person's box can stand in for their face while the face can't be found. An agent reads people with `get_media_analysis`, kind `subjects`.
27	
28	### Salient regions
29	
30	The parts of the picture the eye goes to first, as boxes. In a talking-head shot that's usually the speaker, and on a slide it's often the text. An agent reads them with kind `subjects`, beside the people. See [People and salient regions](/projects/media-analysis/#people-and-salient-regions) under media analysis.
31	
32	[Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) draws all three over the preview, so you can see what Frame Job has to work with.
33	
34	## Boxes, not people
35	
36	Each sample stands alone. A box has no name, and nothing records that a box in one sample is the same person as a box in the next. Frame Job never puts a name to a face, and it doesn't recognise anyone.
37	
38	[Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/#which-subject-it-follows) works out who's who for itself each time, from how the boxes overlap from one sample to the next. That reasoning isn't kept, and it stops at a shot change. Someone who leaves the shot for more than a second and comes back counts as someone new.
39	
40	## When a file is analysed
41	
42	Importing a file doesn't look for any of this. It's found when something asks for it:
43	
44	- **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**
45	- **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**
46	- [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/one-microphone/), when it cuts from faces
47	- An agent, with `get_media_analysis`, `reframe_clip`, `make_vertical_version` or `switch_by_speaker`
48	
49	Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and `reframe_clip` ask only for the part of the file each clip plays, plus a second either side. **View ▸ Show Subjects** never asks, so turning it on costs nothing.
50	
51	Analysis runs in the background and saves what it has found every 30 seconds, so stopping it keeps what's been saved. Asking again continues from there, and a part that's already been analysed isn't read again. What's found is kept in the project's cache. A change to the file, or a macOS update, means it's analysed again.
52	
53	[On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-happens-on-demand) covers this in full, along with everything else Frame Job analyses on your Mac, including [the Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) and [how background jobs run](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-runs-in-the-background).
54	
55	## What uses it
56	
57	| Feature | What it uses |
58	| --- | --- |
59	| [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) | Faces, people and salient regions, to frame the selected clips |
60	| [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) | The same, to frame a whole timeline on a tall or square canvas |
61	| [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/) | Faces and how open each mouth is, to match each microphone to a face |
62	| [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/) | Faces and how open each mouth is, to tell who's talking |
63	| [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) | All three, drawn over the preview |
64	
65	An agent can frame a clip with the same analysis. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/).
66

1	---
2	title: "Copy pieces to another track (agents)"
3	description: How an agent builds a program from synced cameras with copy_pieces, and what it can do with switch_by_speaker that the sheet can't.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	An [agent](/mcp/overview/) can cut a multicam program more directly than the menus do. `copy_pieces` copies parts of a clip onto another track at the same times, and `switch_by_speaker` can preview a cut and use two values the sheet doesn't show. This page is for anyone driving Frame Job from an agent. The exact arguments and results of each tool are in [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="No menu item of its own. Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ and Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker… write with it."
13	  tools={['copy_pieces', 'switch_by_speaker', 'switch_angle']}
14	  needs="Nothing. When there's only one microphone, faces are read on your Mac."
15	/>
16	
17	## Copy pieces of a clip
18	
19	`copy_pieces` takes the parts of one clip between the times you give and puts them on another track at the same times. It's what [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/) and [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) are built from.
20	
21	| Argument | What it does | Required |
22	| --- | --- | --- |
23	| `clip` | The clip to copy from. | Yes |
24	| `track` | The track the pieces land on. It must be free over every range. | Yes |
25	| `ranges` | The stretches to copy, as `[[from, to], …]`, at least one pair. These are times on the timeline, in ticks, 600,000 a second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). | Yes |
26	| `video` | Turns each piece's picture on or off. | No. Default: the clip's own setting. |
27	| `audio` | Turns each piece's sound on or off. | No. Default: the clip's own setting. |
28	
29	The whole call is one undo step, **Copy Pieces**. To work inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/), pass `scope`, and the times and tracks are then the nest's own.
30	
31	### What a piece is
32	
33	Each piece is exactly what splitting the clip at both ends of the range would leave in the middle. It shows the same source frames at the same times, so a piece of a synced camera stays in sync. It keeps the clip's speed, speed ramp, reversal and a graphic's own timeline, and its actions and timed words are cut the way a split cuts them.
34	
35	A piece gets a new id, has no transition, and isn't linked to any detached sound.
36	
37	### How ranges are read
38	
39	- Each range's ends snap to the frame grid.
40	- A pair written backwards is the same range.
41	- A range that's empty on the grid is skipped. If that leaves nothing, nothing changes.
42	- Ranges can touch, but they can't overlap.
43	
44	## Cut a whole program from the cameras
45	
46	An agent cuts a whole program with one `copy_pieces` per camera clip. The pieces land at the times they came from, so they fall into place around each other.
47	
48	<Steps>
49	
50	1. Add the program track with `add_track`, naming it. With no `index` it goes to the front, in front of the cameras.
51	
52	2. For each camera clip, call `copy_pieces` with that clip, the program track, and every stretch where the camera is on screen. This takes the stretches from 0 to 5 seconds and from 10 to 15 seconds:
53	
54	   ```json
55	   { "clip": 12, "track": 5, "ranges": [[0, 3000000], [6000000, 9000000]], "audio": false }
56	   ```
57	
58	3. If the sound comes from separate microphones, pass `audio: false` as above so the pieces stay silent, and mute the camera tracks with `set_track`, because they keep playing their own sound behind the program.
59	
60	</Steps>
61	
62	A range has to sit inside the one clip, so a camera that stopped and started needs a call for each of its clips.
63	
64	To change one shot afterwards, use `switch_angle`, the agent's form of [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/). See [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).
65	
66	## When a copy won't happen
67	
68	Nothing changes when one of these stops the copy. Frame Job checks them in this order and reports the first it meets:
69	
70	1. The clip is a nest. A piece of a nest would replay the nest from its first frame.
71	2. A range falls outside the clip.
72	3. Two ranges overlap.
73	4. The destination track is locked.
74	5. The destination track holds a clip over one of the ranges. The error names that clip and where it starts and ends. The clip you're copying from counts, so a piece can't land on its own track over itself.
75	
76	A copy that would take the project past 4,096 clips also fails.
77	
78	## Switch by Speaker from an agent
79	
80	`switch_by_speaker` cuts a Program track from the selected cameras, with the same values as the [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) sheet and the same result, as one undo step. [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/) explains the values.
81	
82	- Run `sync_audio` first. It trusts where the clips sit and doesn't check that they're in sync.
83	- Set the clips with `set_selection`, because it reads the selected clips.
84	- Every argument is optional, including who's who (`speakers`), the range (`from` and `to`) and the track to replace (`track`).
85	- The sheet pulls a number back into its range. The tool stops with an error instead, and nothing changes.
86	- To work inside a nest, open it with `set_scope` first, because the tool doesn't take `scope`.
87	
88	### Preview the cut
89	
90	Pass `apply: false` to see the shots without editing anything. The result lists each shot's camera, start and end, how many edits it would make and how many clips it would add, and nothing in the project moves. It's the same work as a real run, so it stops for the same reasons.
91	
92	The result has `applied: false` and no `step`, and `track` is null unless you named one. Leave `apply` out and the edit is made.
93	
94	### Values only an agent can set
95	
96	| Argument | What it does | Default | Range |
97	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
98	| `min_turn` | The shortest turn that cuts. A shorter turn, such as a quick reply, starts no shot. | 1 s | 0.2 to 10 s |
99	| `dominance_db` | How far one active microphone must lead every other to count alone. Below that lead, two active microphones are crosstalk. | 8 dB | 0 to 30 dB |
100	
101	### Check which mode ran
102	
103	Every result has a `mode`, either `microphones` or `faces`.
104	
105	Faces mode is [cutting from one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/). You get it by naming one microphone for two or more cameras, and it's the default when the selection holds exactly one microphone. In this mode:
106	
107	- The result's `note` reads "Faces guess who is talking; check the cuts."
108	- `min_shot` is 3 s unless you give it.
109	- A camera you name as `wide` takes no part in deciding who's talking.
110	
111	### Waiting for faces
112	
113	Where **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** would show the Analyzing sheet first, the tool waits for the faces, for up to 60 seconds. Past that it stops with nothing switched, and what it found is kept. Call it again to continue.
114	
115	If the analysis fails or is stopped, or the project changes during the wait, nothing is switched either.
116	
117	### When Switch by Speaker won't run
118	
119	If any of these applies, the call stops and nothing changes. Frame Job checks this first group together and names every one that applies, so you can fix them in one go:
120	
121	- Under two cameras, or over nine. A camera here is a track holding a selected clip with a picture.
122	- A person without a microphone or without a camera.
123	- One microphone for two people, outside faces mode.
124	- A microphone still being analysed, or with no speech in the range.
125	- Speech detection isn't available on this Mac.
126	- A camera whose faces are still being found, or that shows no face whose mouth can be read.
127	- A stretch no camera covers.
128	
129	These each stop the call on their own:
130	
131	- A faces analysis that failed, was stopped or ran past the wait.
132	- A project that changed during the wait.
133	- More clips than the project may hold. Raise `min_shot` to make fewer shots.
134	- A track named to replace that can't take the shots: it's locked, it holds a selected clip, it isn't in front of the cameras, it has nothing in the range, or it holds a clip that isn't a piece of a camera.
135	- A camera clip linked to its detached sound. Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first.
136
