2	title: "Cut from faces with one microphone"
3	description: When one microphone hears everyone, let Switch by Speaker decide who is talking from the cameras' pictures, and check the result.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	When one microphone hears everyone, it can't say who's talking. [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) then decides from the cameras' pictures instead, by watching whose mouth is moving.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…"
13	  tools="switch_by_speaker"
14	  needs="Nothing. Face detection and speech detection run on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
15	/>
16	
17	## One microphone for everyone
18	
19	Frame Job works this way when your selection holds exactly one microphone and two or more cameras. That includes a selection where only one camera has sound. See [Microphones](/multicam/set-up/#microphones).
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Line the recordings up with **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**.
24	
25	2. Select the cameras' clips and the microphone's clip, then choose **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**.
26	
27	3. If the cameras haven't been read yet, wait for the [Analyzing sheet](#finding-faces-first).
28	
29	4. Check [the sheet](#the-sheet-in-this-mode) and choose **Switch**.
30	
31	5. [Look through the result](#faces-only-guess) and fix any wrong shots.
32	
33	</Steps>
34	
35	While the microphone hears speech, the camera whose person's mouth moves most is shown:
36	
37	- Each camera's person is the largest face in its picture.
38	- Frame Job watches that mouth opening and closing over half a second.
39	- A camera wins when its mouth moves at least half as much again as the next camera's (1.5×) and more than a small minimum.
40	- When two mouths move alike, or the busiest mouth stays under that minimum, it's crosstalk, and [**Crosstalk**](/multicam/switch-settings/#crosstalk-shows) decides what shows.
41	- With no speech, or no mouth to read, the current shot holds.
42	
43	The rest of the cut works as it does with several microphones, and it writes the same [Program track](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/#the-program-track) as one undo step.
44	
45	## Finding faces first
46	
47	Frame Job reads faces from its [on-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/) of each camera. When a camera's faces haven't been found yet, an **Analyzing** sheet comes up first, with a bar for each file. The Switch by Speaker sheet opens once they're found.
48	
49	Only the part of each camera the range needs is analysed, and what's found is kept in the project's cache, so next time it's quicker or skipped.
50	
51	| If | Then |
52	| --- | --- |
53	| You choose **Stop** | Everything stays as it was, and what was saved so far is kept. Frame Job saves as it goes, every 30 seconds. Choose the command again to carry on. |
54	| The analysis fails | Frame Job beeps and says why at the foot of the inspector. |
55	| The project changed while it analysed | Frame Job beeps, says so at the foot of the inspector, and switches nothing. Choose the command again. |
56	
57	## The sheet in this mode
58	
59	The sheet changes to suit one microphone:
60	
61	- One **Microphone:** pop-up replaces the speaker rows, and **Cameras:** lists every camera.
62	- There's no **Ignore bleed** row, because there's no second microphone to bleed into.
63	- **Minimum shot** opens at 3 s, not 2 s, and isn't remembered.
64	- **Wide** opens on **None**.
65	
66	The other rows work as they do in [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/).
67	
68	A camera with no face whose mouth can be read stops the cut. The summary reads "The camera on track … shows no face whose mouth can be read between … and …, so it never says who is talking." A camera whose faces still aren't found reads "The camera on track … is still being analysed — its faces have not been found yet. Try again in a moment."
69	
70	## Wide in this mode
71	
72	Choose a **Wide** to show it during crosstalk. That camera then takes no part in deciding who talks, so a true wide shot whose faces are too small to read won't stop the cut. With no Wide, crosstalk holds the current shot.
73	
74	With only two cameras, making one the Wide leaves a single camera for faces to decide between. Faces no longer decide and the warning leaves the summary. The cut then opens on the Wide, moves to the other camera at the first turn of speech, and stays there unless [**Cut to the wide after**](/multicam/switch-settings/#cut-to-the-wide-after) breaks it up.
75	
76	## Faces only guess
77	
78	The summary starts "Faces guess who is talking; check the cuts."
79	
80	Frame Job measures only how much each mouth moves while the microphone hears speech, so a mouth that moves without speaking, such as laughing or chewing, can put a cut in the wrong place. A face turned away gives no mouth to read, so that camera can't be chosen while it's turned, even if that person is the one talking. Look through the result and fix those shots with [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).
81	
82	## Good to know
83	
84	- Only the largest face in a camera is read. With two people in one shot, the other person's mouth doesn't count.
85	- Only video files are read for faces. A still picture on a camera track has no mouth to read.
86	- Pointing every speaker row at one microphone in the ordinary sheet also reads faces. It doesn't bring up the Analyzing sheet, so a camera not yet read stays "still being analysed". To find its faces, change the selection so it comes to [one microphone](/multicam/set-up/#microphones), and choose the command again.
87	
88	## With an agent
89	
90	There's no Analyzing sheet for `switch_by_speaker`. The call waits up to 60 seconds for the faces, then stops, keeping what was saved so far, and calling it again carries on. Its answer says which way it decided and repeats the warning. See [Copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/).
91

2	title: "Set up several cameras"
3	description: Put each camera on its own track, line them up by their sound, name them, and get a program track ready for a show filmed with more than one camera.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Set up a show filmed with several cameras, such as a podcast with a camera on each guest or an interview with a wide and a close shot, so you can cut between them.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio', 'Clip ▸ Split']}
13	  keys={['⌘T']}
14	  tools={['sync_audio', 'copy_pieces']}
15	/>
16	
17	## How multicam works
18	
19	There's no special multicam clip. Each camera is an ordinary clip on an ordinary track, and the edit you watch is a **program track** in front of them, made of pieces of whichever camera you want at each moment.
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Put [one camera on each track](#one-camera-per-track) and line them up.
24	2. [Name the tracks](#name-the-tracks) after their cameras.
25	3. Build [the program track](#the-program-track), by hand or with [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/).
26	4. Fix single shots with [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).
27	
28	</Steps>
29	
30	## One camera per track
31	
32	Put each camera's recording on a track of its own, then line the recordings up in time. **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** does this from their sound: select the recordings and choose it. See [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).
33	
34	If a camera stopped and started again, its pieces can all sit on the one track.
35	
36	## Name the tracks
37	
38	Double-click a track's header and type the camera's name. These names are what **Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸** lists, and what the Switch by Speaker sheet uses for its cameras and microphones.
39	
40	When two listed tracks share a name, Frame Job adds each one's position counted from the back, for example "Camera (2)" and "Camera (3)".
41	
42	## The program track
43	
44	[Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) can write the whole program track for you, and it adds its own track.
45	
46	To build the program by hand:
47	
48	<Steps>
49	
50	1. Move the playhead to the start of a camera's clip.
51	2. Select the clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>, then <kbd>⌘V</kbd>. A copy can't sit on top of its original, so it lands on a new track in front of the others, at the playhead, in sync with the camera. That track is your program.
52	3. With the copy selected, move the playhead to a cut and choose **Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>). Repeat for each cut, selecting the piece the cut falls in each time.
53	4. Select a shot and pick another camera from [**Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**](/multicam/switch-angle/).
54	
55	</Steps>
56	
57	The paste makes the track itself, so you don't need **Track ▸ New Track** (<kbd>⇧⌘N</kbd>) here. A track you added first would stay empty behind the copy.
58	
59	A pasted copy keeps its sound on, so the same sound plays from the program track and the camera's track until you [mute one of them](/audio/mute-and-solo/). The pieces Switch by Speaker writes have their sound off.
60	
61	An agent builds the program with one `copy_pieces` call per camera. See [Copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/).
62	
63	## Shown or hidden
64	
65	The camera tracks stay underneath the program. Leave them shown and the program track, being in front, covers them. Or hide them with the hide switch in the track header, or **Hide Video** in the header's right-click menu. See [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).
66	
67	Either way they still work as cameras: a hidden track's clips are still listed by Switch Angle and still count for Switch by Speaker.
68	
69	## Microphones
70	
71	Switch by Speaker needs to know which recording hears which person. It works this out from what you've selected.
72	
73	| Selected | What counts as a microphone |
74	| --- | --- |
75	| Clips with their sound on and no picture, such as a recorder or a separate microphone file | Every track holding one |
76	| No clips like that | Each camera that plays sound is its own microphone |
77	| A camera's sound split off with **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** | Never chosen for you, but you can pick it in a **Microphone** pop-up |
78	
79	So keep each person's microphone file on a track of its own, beside the cameras, and select it with them. Only the selected clips on a microphone's track are listened to.
80	
81	The sheet's **Microphone** pop-ups list every track holding a selected clip with its sound on, so you can swap in a detached camera sound or a camera's own sound there. An agent can name a detached camera sound as a microphone too.
82	
83	When the selection comes to exactly one microphone and two or more cameras, Switch by Speaker can't tell people apart by ear, so it decides from their faces. That includes the case where only one camera has sound. See [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/).
84

2	title: "Switch Angle"
3	description: Re-pick one shot of your program from another camera, in sync, over exactly the same span.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Switch Angle replaces one shot with another camera's picture over exactly the same span. Use it to fix a single cut after [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/), or to pick shots by hand. Your cameras need to be [lined up on tracks of their own](/multicam/set-up/) first.
10	
11	<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸" tools="switch_angle" />
12	
13	## Switch to another camera
14	
15	<Steps>
16	
17	1. Select the one shot you want to change, usually a clip on your [program track](/multicam/set-up/#the-program-track).
18	
19	2. Open **Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**. The submenu [lists the cameras](#the-camera-list) that cover the whole shot.
20	
21	3. Choose a camera.
22	
23	</Steps>
24	
25	The whole switch is one undo step, called **Switch Angle**. The new clip is selected afterwards, or all of them if the shot became [several pieces](#a-camera-that-stopped-and-started). Switch Angle has no keyboard shortcut.
26	
27	## The camera list
28	
29	The submenu lists, front track first, every other track whose video clips cover the shot's whole span. Frame Job writes the list each time the menu opens, so it always matches the current selection.
30	
31	- Only clips of a video file with a picture count. Pictures, freeze frames, text, shapes, graphics and nests don't.
32	- A clip with its picture switched off still counts, and so does a clip on a hidden track. That's what keeps your cameras in the list after [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) has hidden them or turned their pictures off.
33	- The list stops at nine tracks. A tenth covering track, further back, isn't listed.
34	
35	### Tracks with the same name
36	
37	When two listed tracks share a name, each gets its position counted from the back track, for example **Camera (2)** and **Camera (3)**. A name only one listed track has appears as it is.
38	
39	### No Covering Angle
40	
41	The submenu holds a single greyed item, **No Covering Angle**, when there's nothing to switch to. That happens when you haven't selected exactly one clip, or when no track covers the selected clip. This item is never available.
42	
43	### Greyed cameras
44	
45	The cameras are listed but greyed when the switch can't be made:
46	
47	| Why it's greyed | What to do |
48	| --- | --- |
49	| The shot's track is locked. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
50	| The shot is linked to a detached sound. | Choose [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
51	| A sheet is open on the window. | Close the sheet. |
52	
53	## What the switch does
54	
55	The shot is replaced by the camera's picture on the shot's own track, over the same span and in sync. The new clip shows the camera's own frame at every moment, so a cut to it lands exactly where the old shot's cut did.
56	
57	### A camera that stopped and started
58	
59	A shot can cross the end of one of the camera's clips and the start of the next, when the camera stopped and started again. The shot then becomes two pieces, one from each file, meeting at a plain cut. A shot that crosses more of the camera's clips gets one piece for each.
60	
61	### Overlapping camera clips
62	
63	Where two of a camera's clips overlap, as they do across a transition, the later one takes over at its own start. The shot gets a piece of each, meeting at a plain cut, so a transition between those two clips doesn't appear in the shot.
64	
65	## What the shot keeps and loses
66	
67	The shot keeps:
68	
69	- Its span on the timeline.
70	- Whether its picture and its sound are on. A shot with its sound off gives you a new clip with its sound off, whatever the camera's clip has.
71	- The [transitions](/motion/transitions/) at both of its edges, with their kind, curve and audio shape.
72	
73	Nothing else carries over. A punch-in, a grade or an action on the old shot isn't copied to the new camera's piece. The piece is cut from the camera's own clip, so it has that clip's settings instead.
74	
75	## A transition that no longer fits
76	
77	A transition needs the two clips to overlap by its length. When the camera's first or last piece is too short for that, Frame Job drops that transition and makes the switch anyway, leaving a plain cut at that edge. The undo step then reads **Switch Angle (transition removed)**, so you can see that it happened.
78	
79	## When a switch fails
80	
81	When a switch can't be done, nothing changes. Frame Job beeps and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, after the word "Refused:". The message gives clips and tracks by number, and times in ticks, 600,000 to the second.
82	
83	| The message says | What it means |
84	| --- | --- |
85	| "clip 7's edge is held at tick …, short of tick …, so clip 9 cannot be re-picked" | The clip next to the shot plays a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) that can't give up the transition's frames. The message names that clip and the shot. |
86	| "track 3 does not cover clip 12: nothing with a picture plays on it at tick …" | The camera doesn't cover the shot, and the message names the first moment it doesn't. The menu only lists cameras that cover the shot, so this one normally comes back to an agent calling `switch_angle`. |
87	
88	## Good to know
89	
90	- Switch Angle works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), on the nest's own tracks.
91	- Only the shot's track has to be unlocked. A locked camera track is still listed, and you can switch to it.
92	- Frame Job doesn't check what kind of clip you've selected. A text or picture clip with a camera covering it gets replaced in the same way.
93	- A shot that becomes several pieces adds clips. At the project's limit of 4,096 clips, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes, with no message.
94	
95	## With an agent
96	
97	`switch_angle` makes the same switch, and it takes the shot and the camera's track directly, so an agent isn't held to the menu's nine tracks. It returns the new clips rather than selecting them. To work inside a nest, open it with `set_scope` first, because the tool doesn't take `scope`. See [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).
98	
99	To lay a whole program out at once rather than one shot at a time, an agent can use [`copy_pieces`](/multicam/copy-pieces/).
100	
101	## Related
102	
103	- [Set up several cameras](/multicam/set-up/)
104	- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
105	- [Transitions](/motion/transitions/)
106	- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
107	- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)
108	- [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/)
109

1	---
2	title: "Switch by Speaker"
3	description: Cut a whole Program track from a conversation, showing whoever is talking on each microphone, as one undo step.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Switch by Speaker cuts a whole program for you from a conversation. It listens to each person's microphone and writes a new track that shows whoever is talking.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…"
14	  tools="switch_by_speaker"
15	  needs="Nothing. It reads each microphone's loudness and speech detection, made on your Mac at import, with no key and no upload."
16	/>
17	
18	## Cut a conversation
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. [Synchronize the recordings](#synchronize-first) with **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**.
23	
24	2. Select every camera's clips and every microphone's clips. <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click each clip to add it, or <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag a band across them. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
25	
26	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**. It has no keyboard shortcut, and it sits right after Synchronize Audio in the **Clip** menu.
27	
28	4. Check the [speaker rows](#speaker-rows) and adjust the [settings](/multicam/switch-settings/) if you need to. The [summary](#the-summary) at the foot of the sheet updates as you do.
29	
30	5. Choose **Switch** or press Return. **Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> leaves everything as it was.
31	
32	</Steps>
33	
34	<Shot
35	  name="15h-switch-by-speaker-sheet.sheet"
36	  alt="The Switch by Speaker sheet. Two speaker rows pair the Camera microphone with the Camera track and the Screen microphone with the Screen track. Below them are Wide set to None, Minimum shot 2 s, Cut 0.2 s before speech, Crosstalk shows Wide, Ignore bleed 15 dB, two unticked boxes, and the summary 1 shot: 1 on Camera. Adds 1 clip."
37	/>
38	
39	Afterwards, [fix single shots](#fix-the-result) by hand. Switch by Speaker works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/) too, on the nest's own tracks.
40	
41	## Synchronize first
42	
43	Switch by Speaker trusts where the clips sit. It doesn't check that they're in sync, so run [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) before it.
44	
45	A camera [slipped](/editing/slip-and-roll/) or dragged afterwards puts its shots out of step with the voices.
46	
47	## When it is offered
48	
49	**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** is available when:
50	
51	- the selection holds clips with a picture on two or more tracks, each of which is a camera
52	- at least one selected clip has its sound on, from a file that has sound
53	- no sheet is open on the window
54	
55	Sound you've split off with **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** never makes its track a camera. The sheet handles up to nine cameras. The command is still offered with more, but the summary then says so and **Switch** stays dimmed.
56	
57	## Speaker rows
58	
59	Each person gets a row, reading **Speaker 1:**, then a microphone pop-up, the word "on", and the camera that shows them. A camera that is its own microphone stays paired with itself, and the rest are paired front to back to start with. See [Microphones](/multicam/set-up/#microphones) for how the microphones are chosen.
60	
61	Each person needs their own microphone and a camera. A pop-up offers **None** only where the selection left that row with nothing to pair. Leave it on **None** and the summary says what's missing.
62	
63	Change the rows when the front-to-back guess puts someone on the wrong camera. The microphones listed come from your selection, and the cameras from the tracks holding your selected pictures.
64	
65	With exactly one microphone and two or more cameras, the rows are replaced by a different layout. See [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/).
66	
67	## The range
68	
69	The cut covers the [In–Out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) when one is set, otherwise the whole length of the selected camera clips.
70	
71	Only the selected clips of a microphone's track are listened to. A camera track offers all its clips with a picture, selected or not, so an unselected clip on a camera track can still supply shots.
72	
73	## The summary
74	
75	The line under the controls says what **Switch** will do, for example "22 shots: 8 on Cam A, 14 on Cam B. Adds 23 clips." Cameras appear in the order they first show.
76	
77	When Switch can't go ahead, every reason replaces that line, one per line, and **Switch** stays dimmed. The sheet works this out again at every change, so change any control to check again.
78	
79	| The summary says | What it means |
80	| --- | --- |
81	| "The microphone on track … is still being analysed…" | Frame Job hasn't finished measuring that file's loudness or detecting its speech, which can happen straight after an import. Give it a moment, then change any control to check again. |
82	| "The microphone on track … has no speech between … and …, so it never says who is talking." | That microphone hears no speech in the range. Check you've paired the right track, or shorten the range. |
83	| "No angle has a picture between … and …." | No camera covers that stretch of the range. Set an In–Out range that avoids it, or fill the gap. |
84	| "The speaker on track … has no microphone." | A row has no microphone that's selected and sounding. |
85	| "The microphone on track … has no angle to show its speaker." | A row has no camera. |
86	| "Track … is the microphone for 2 speakers; each person needs their own microphone." | One microphone is on two rows. See [Good to know](#good-to-know) for when that's allowed. |
87	| "Switch by Speaker takes at most nine angles…" | More than nine tracks hold a selected picture. Select fewer. |
88	| "Switch by Speaker would add … clips to …; the most is 4096 — raise the minimum shot." | A project holds at most 4,096 clips. Raise [**Minimum shot**](/multicam/switch-settings/#minimum-shot) for fewer, longer shots. |
89	| "Speech detection is unavailable on this Mac, so Switch by Speaker cannot tell who is talking." | The on-device speech model can't run here, so the command can't work. |
90	| "The project's audio plan could not be read. Try again in a moment." | Frame Job couldn't read the project's sound just then. |
91	
92	An "angle" in these lines is a camera. The track number is Frame Job's own number for the track, not its position on the timeline. With one shared microphone, [two more lines](/multicam/one-microphone/#the-sheet-in-this-mode) can appear.
93	
94	**Switch** checks everything once more when you press it. If it can't go ahead at that moment, the reason shows in the summary and the sheet stays open.
95	
96	## How it chooses the shots
97	
98	- A cut lands a moment before each new speaker's first word. [**Cut**](/multicam/switch-settings/#cut-before-speech) sets how long.
99	- Silence holds the current shot, and so does a reply under a second long.
100	- A pause under half a second between one person's words doesn't end their turn.
101	- The cut opens on the [Wide](/multicam/switch-settings/#wide), the camera you've chosen for your wide shot, when there is one, otherwise on the first speaker's camera. With no Wide and nobody taking a turn, the range is one shot on the front-most camera.
102	- When two people talk at once, [**Crosstalk**](/multicam/switch-settings/#crosstalk-shows) decides what shows.
103	- Where a shot's camera has nothing to show, that stretch goes to the Wide, else the camera before it, else the front-most camera that covers it.
104	- A shot under [**Minimum shot**](/multicam/switch-settings/#minimum-shot) merges into a neighbour.
105	
106	## Linked cameras
107	
108	A camera clip still linked to its detached sound can't be switched. The sheet says so and names the clip, ending "Attach Audio first". Choose [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) to put the two back together, then try again.
109	
110	Only a linked camera clip crossing the range stops the cut.
111	
112	## One undo step
113	
114	**Switch** writes all of this as one undo step, **Switch by Speaker**. The selection stays. A selected clip cut at the range's ends brings its new half into the selection.
115	
116	### The Program track
117	
118	Switch adds a track named **Program** directly in front of the front-most camera. It holds a piece of the chosen camera for each shot, in sync, with the picture on and the sound off.
119	
120	To write over an earlier Program track instead, use [**Write to**](/multicam/switch-settings/#write-to).
121	
122	### Cameras hidden
123	
124	Switch hides the camera tracks so only the program shows.
125	
126	A camera track that holds anything outside the range, or any clip without a picture, isn't hidden. Its clips are cut at the range's ends and their pictures are switched off inside the range only.
127	
128	### What stays untouched
129	
130	Nothing outside the range changes. The microphones aren't edited, so what you hear stays the same, apart from any camera sound you chose to [mute](/multicam/switch-settings/#mute-the-cameras-own-sound).
131	
132	## Fix the result
133	
134	- To show a different camera for one shot, select the shot and use [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).
135	- To move a cut, [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/) it.
136	- To try other settings, choose **Switch by Speaker…** again while the clips are still selected, and pick the old track under **Write to**. Or undo and start over.
137	
138	## Good to know
139	
140	- One microphone on two rows stops the cut when other rows have their own microphones. If you point every row at one microphone, Frame Job reads faces instead, and the summary starts with its [warning](/multicam/one-microphone/#faces-only-guess).
141	- Switch by Speaker doesn't remember your pairing. The speaker rows open fresh each time.
142	
143	## With an agent
144	
145	`switch_by_speaker` takes the sheet's values and a few it doesn't show. An agent can name the range directly, which takes priority over the In–Out range, and pair people by hand. It can also ask for the shots without editing anything, and set the shortest turn that cuts and how far one microphone must lead to count alone. See [Copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/) and [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).
146	
147	## Related
148	
149	- [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/)
150	- [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)
151	- [Set up several cameras](/multicam/set-up/)
152	- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
153	- [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/)
154

1	---
2	title: "Switch by Speaker settings"
3	description: What each row of the Switch by Speaker sheet does, its default and range, and which values Frame Job remembers.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These rows of the [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) sheet shape the cut: where it opens, how long shots last, and how it treats two people talking at once.
9	
10	<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…" tools="switch_by_speaker" />
11	
12	| Row | What it does | Default | Range |
13	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
14	| [**Wide:**](#wide) | Your wide shot, which opens the cut and shows during crosstalk | The one camera no person uses, otherwise None | Any camera, or None |
15	| [**Minimum shot:**](#minimum-shot) | The shortest shot allowed | 2 s (3 s with [one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)) | 0.5 to 30 s |
16	| [**Cut:**](#cut-before-speech) | How long before speech the cut comes | 0.2 s | 0 to 1 s |
17	| [**Crosstalk:**](#crosstalk-shows) | What shows while two people talk at once | Wide | Wide, Current speaker |
18	| [**Ignore bleed:**](#ignore-bleed) | How far below a speaker's level a voice is ignored | 15 dB | 3 to 40 dB |
19	| [**Cut to the wide after**](#cut-to-the-wide-after) | Breaks up a long monologue | Off | 2 to 600 s |
20	| [**Mute the cameras' own sound**](#mute-the-cameras-own-sound) | Turns the cameras' sound off inside the range | On when no microphone is on a camera track | |
21	| [**Write to:**](#write-to) | Where the cut goes | A new Program track | |
22	
23	The number fields take up to two decimal places.
24	
25	## Wide
26	
27	The camera for your wide shot. Choose any of the cameras, or **None**. If exactly one camera is left over once every person has theirs, it's picked to start with. Otherwise the row opens on **None**.
28	
29	The Wide shows:
30	
31	- at the start of the cut
32	- during crosstalk, when [**Crosstalk**](#crosstalk-shows) shows **Wide**
33	- after [**Cut to the wide after**](#cut-to-the-wide-after)
34	- for a stretch where another camera has nothing to show
35	
36	When nobody is talking, the current shot holds. It doesn't go to the Wide.
37	
38	## Minimum shot
39	
40	The shortest shot the cut may have, from 0.5 to 30 s. The default is 2 s.
41	
42	A shorter shot merges into the shot before it when that camera covers the stretch, otherwise into the shot after it. A short shot that neither neighbour covers stays.
43	
44	Raising this is also the way out when the cut would add more clips than a project can hold.
45	
46	## Cut before speech
47	
48	The **Cut:** row sets how long before a new speaker's first word the cut comes, from 0 to 1 s. The default is 0.2 s, and the cut lands on a whole frame.
49	
50	## Late cuts under heavy bleed
51	
52	A cut is timed from where a voice first rises above its [bleed](#ignore-bleed) line and the microphone's quiet background, not from the word itself. So with heavy bleed in a noisy room, a cut can land later than **Cut** asks. In the worst case measured, with another voice 24 dB down under −45 dBFS of noise, the cut came about 35 ms before the first word instead of 0.2 s.
53	
54	## Crosstalk shows
55	
56	What the program shows while two people talk at once for a second or more. **Wide** cuts to the [Wide](#wide), and **Current speaker** holds the shot you're on. With no Wide chosen, crosstalk holds the current shot whatever this says.
57	
58	Crosstalk shorter than a second starts nothing. A stretch under half a second between two bursts of crosstalk counts as crosstalk.
59	
60	Two microphones are crosstalk when both hear a voice above their [bleed](#ignore-bleed) line. If one leads the other by 8 dB or more, measured against each one's own speaker, it counts alone.
61	
62	## Ignore bleed
63	
64	Every microphone also hears the other people, quieter. A voice more than this far below a microphone's own speaker is bleed, and never counts as that person talking. It runs from 3 to 40 dB, and the default is 15 dB.
65	
66	- Raise it if a quiet guest is never shown.
67	- Lower it if someone is shown while only the other person talks.
68	
69	A voice must also stand 6 dB above the microphone's quiet background to count. This row doesn't appear in the [one-microphone sheet](/multicam/one-microphone/#the-sheet-in-this-mode).
70	
71	## Cut to the wide after
72	
73	Breaks up a long monologue. Tick the box and set how long one person may hold the screen, from 2 to 600 s. It's off by default, and the field offers 20 s.
74	
75	When a shot reaches that length, the Wide shows for one [**Minimum shot**](#minimum-shot), then the speaker's camera returns. This repeats to the end of the shot.
76	
77	It needs a Wide. With **Wide** on **None**, ticking it does nothing.
78	
79	## Mute the cameras' own sound
80	
81	Switches the cameras' scratch sound, the rough sound each camera recorded for itself, off inside the range. It's ticked to start with when no microphone is on a camera track, which is when the microphones are separate recordings.
82	
83	It never touches a microphone's track, so a camera used as a microphone keeps its sound.
84	
85	## Write to
86	
87	Writes the new cut over an earlier Program track instead of adding another. Choose **Replace the shots on** and the track's name, or leave it on **A new Program track**, the default.
88	
89	The row shows only when an earlier track can be replaced. That track must:
90	
91	- be unlocked
92	- hold no selected clip
93	- sit in front of the cameras
94	- have something in the range
95	- hold only pieces of the cameras there
96	
97	The track is cleared over the range and cut at its ends. Nothing on it outside the range changes.
98	
99	## Remembered values
100	
101	**Minimum shot**, **Cut**, **Crosstalk** and **Ignore bleed** are kept for the next time. They're written only when you change a value and press **Switch**, so **Cancel** keeps the old ones.
102	
103	**Minimum shot** isn't remembered in the one-microphone sheet. Every other row opens fresh each time. An agent's call reads none of the remembered values and uses the defaults in the table above.
104	
105	## With an agent
106	
107	`switch_by_speaker` takes these rows as `wide`, `min_shot`, `lead`, `crosstalk`, `bleed_db`, `wide_after`, `mute_cameras` and `track`. See [its options](/mcp/tools-multicam/#switch-by-speaker-options).
108	
109	## Related
110	
111	- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
112	- [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)
113	- [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/)
114	- [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/)

Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/CLAUDE.md:

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

//! (`reframe_cover.rs`).
//!
//! **The frames.** A box is 0…1 of the upright picture from its top-left. Its
//! point `(bx, by)` is `u = (bx·mw − mw/2, by·mh − mh/2)` px from the
//! UNCROPPED centre (`mw × mh` the media's displayed size), and lands on the
//! source canvas at `anchor + s·u` — `edit_zoom.rs`'s (★) at θ = 0, with
//! `anchor` and `s` the clip's base `video`. A crop moves only the
//! picture's extent, the cropped rect `anchor + s·(c ± (cw/2, ch/2))`, so
//! the analysis cache never depends on it.

//! **The window.** The part of the source canvas the target shows: `W/k ×
//! H/k`, where `k·s` is `zoom ×` the fill scale of the cropped picture on

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
  action's end instead of interpolating.
- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points
  (`CurvePoint`), the FIELD `VideoProps.curves` written only when not the identity
  (`curve_is_identity`: every y = x, from x 0 to x 1); format 20 (GR-32) adds `hue_hue` and
  `hue_sat` (`[hue, value]` points, 0 ≤ hue < 360) and `CurveDomain` (each channel's identity,
  neutral and value range; `named()` and `named_mut()` give each channel's), a hue curve the
  identity when every value is its neutral; `actions_curves.rs`'s `curves_json` writes all
  six, an absent one as its domain's identity. Format 18 (GR-13) adds `Qualifier {hue,
  saturation, luma, invert}` (`HueRange {center, width, softness}` in degrees, `LevelRange
  {low, high, softness}` 0–1, a range `None` when off), the FIELD `VideoProps.qualifier`,
  written only when not neutral; it acts only on an adjustment clip. Format 21 (GR-35)
  adds `Qualifier.blur` (0…1, written only when above 0, after `invert`) and
  `QUALIFIER_BLUR_MAX`; `is_neutral` counts it, so a blur alone is kept. Re-exported whole
  by `model_props.rs`.
- `cube.rs` — the `.cube` reader (spec §11 GR-8): 3D only, size 2–65, the
  default domain; anything else refused by line and name. `ffi_cube.rs` — the
  four `rc_cube_*` exports. `lut.rs` — a LUT media's rules: placing one is
  refused, removing one clears the looks that name it (the clips stay) and
  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without
  `with_clips`; paste carries it by path. `Project::check_lut_reference` is
  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
- `cursor_file.rs` — the cursor file, format v1 (road map "creator-jobs" CU1a, spec
  §11 CU-10): its module doc IS the format's specification (the header, the columns
  in integer µs and points × 100, the caps, every refusal's sentence, the parse
  order); `RC_CURSOR_FILE_VERSION` (the header's `#define` held to it by
  `core/tests/cursor_file.rs`), the caps, the types and `CursorFile::parse`, which
  reads the object, `format`, `version` and CU-7's `typed` keys loosely BEFORE the
  strict `deny_unknown_fields` read through `serde_path_to_error`, so a newer file is
  refused by its version and a project by its format. `cursor_file_check.rs` — its
  check (`check`, `check_typed`; a shortcut holds `cmd` or `ctrl`, or `opt` with
  `OPTION_SHORTCUT_KEYS`, CU-60) and the base64 decoder, a module of its own because
  the two together pass the 400-line cap for a new file. `ffi_cursor.rs` —
  `rc_cursor_open` (parse and check; an open is the recorder's read-back, CU-15),
  `rc_cursor_free` and `rc_cursor_query` (road map creator-jobs CU2, spec §11 CU-25).
  `cursor_track.rs` — `CursorTrack`, the handle: the parsed file and its prepared
  paths under a `Mutex` (a `state` holds it only to clone an `Arc`, a poisoned lock
  taken with `into_inner`), ticks ↔ µs through `time.rs`, CU-20's M2 mapping per
  geometry entry (`scale_factor`, not `pixels_per_point`; `to_movie`, the one function), the raw path, idle opacity (CU-22),
  the image in force and ripples (CU-23). `cursor_smooth.rs` — `hold_end`, the one
  hold rule, and `SmoothPath` (pins, RDP, centripetal Catmull–Rom; CU-21).

  authority — the enum's fields are, and `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves
  every row by asking the decoder. Capped at 400 lines like any new module:
  it does NOT inherit `edit.rs`'s table exemption.
- `op_schema.rs` — `op_table.rs` written as JSON Schema, which is what
  `rc_op_schemas` publishes (road map 7's D3·2): one object per op, its
  properties the arguments and its `required` the ones the decoder will not
  do without. **The match over `Kind` is exhaustive** — a kind added to the
  table does not compile until this says what JSON it is — and it is a
  module of its own because a row changes when an OP does and this changes
  when the published DIALECT does. It says nothing about what an argument is
  FOR (the catalog's prose), nothing about what a patch may CARRY
  (`Kind::Object` is an object with no properties; D1 left the core the one
  validator of that), and nothing about `additionalProperties` on an op,
  because the catalog merges `project` and `scope` in afterwards. Tested
  through the FFI in `core/tests/op_schemas.rs`.

  VIEW project from the nest (its tracks and clips at top level, its frozen
  size as the canvas, the parent's rate, media, `next_id` and nests, no
  markers), applies the op to it UNCHANGED, merges back. So `Project::clip`
  keeps its one meaning and no op has a nest-aware branch. Three things are
  counter-intuitive and measured: the scoped nest's own row stays in the view
  with its tracks and clips EMPTIED (removing it dangles every other nest's
  reference; leaving it whole doubles every id under `validate`); the nests
  write-back is union first, orphans after; and **a scoped apply has a wider
  `Err` arm than any unscoped op** — `check_caps` and `check_nesting` are
  document-wide and run on the MERGED parent, so an op valid inside the nest
  can still return `Err`. `refused_inside` is an EXHAUSTIVE match over every
  op, so a new op does not compile until it is classified; `set_media_cursor`
  is refused inside like `set_media_speech` (twelve ops in all, `edit.rs`'s
  module doc). The READ half is
  `rc_project_scoped` in `ffi.rs`, which calls the same `scoped_view`.

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

//! The framing planner (road map "creator-jobs" VR2a1, spec §11 VR-20,

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,

  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:

  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11

  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only

  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:

  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in

  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
